1.    Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited.

Heritage Hills Operator LLC d/b/a Heritage Hills Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center (“Heritage
Hills” or “Applicant”) seeks approval for the acquisition of Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation
Center, a 100 bed licensed skilled nursing facility located at 80 Douglas Pike, Smithfield, Rhode
Island (the “Facility”). Pursuant to the terms of 1) the Asset Purchase Agreement as amended on
October 15, 2021 by and among Health Concepts Ltd. (“Health Concepts”), Trinity Square, LLC,
River View Nursing Home Inc. d/b/a River View Health Care Community, Village House
Convalescent Home, Inc. d/b/a Village Health Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, Village House
Convalescent Home Associates LLC, Elmwood Health Center, Inc. d/b/a Elmwood Health Center,
David M. Ryan, Sally J. Ryan, Elmwood Avenue Realty LLC, Ryan Health Center Inc. d/b/a
Morgan Health Center, 76 Morgan, LLC, Westerly Health Center Associates Limited Partnership
d/b/a Westerly Health Center, Burrillville Health Center Associates Limited Partnership d/b/a
Bayberry Commons, Warwick Health Centre, Inc. d/b/a West Shore Health Center, Wellshore
Properties, LLC, Allen’s Health Center Inc. d/b/a South Kingstown Nursing & Rehabilitation
Center, 80 Douglas Pike LLC d/b/a Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, 198 Waterman
Avenue LLC d/b/a Eastgate Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, Ryan Finance, LLC (collectively, the
“Sellers”) and RSO Investments, LLC (the “Buyer”), 2) an Operations Transfer Agreement made
and entered on the July 8, 2021 by and between 80 Douglas Pike LLC (“Old Operator”) and Shore
Point Holdings, LLC, and 3) the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement by and between
Rainwood Holdings LLC, Bayberry Rehabilitation & Nursing LLC, RSO Investments LLC,
Garden Property Holdings LLC, Lakeland Equities LLC, RSO Holdings LLC, Shore Point Equities
LLC, Shore Point Investments LLC and Brick Garden Equities LLC, (the “Proposed Transaction”)
all of the Facility’s assets including its real estate and operating assets will be conveyed to Heritage
Hills Property LLC (“Heritage Hills Property”) and Heritage Hills, respectively. Heritage Hills
Property will enter into a lease agreement with Heritage Hill. A copy of the Proposed Transaction
agreements and lease are attached at Tabs 14 and 24, respectively. As part of the Proposed
Transaction, the Applicant and its affiliates seek to acquire a total of four Rhode Island facilities
(and are filing four CEC Applications) all currently owned and operated by Health Concepts
entities:

- Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center
- Morgan Health Center
- Riverview Healthcare Community
- Westerly Health Center

The total purchase price allocation for the acquisition of the operations and real estate of the
Facility is $6,920,543.00. The Applicant anticipates it will fund the purchase price as follows: 1)
$1,384,109.00 from the Applicant’s cash on hand, which will represent a 20% equity position and 2)
$5,536,434.00 in the form of a loan, which will represent an 80% debt position.

The Applicant is wholly owned by Quinto Nexgen LLC (“Quinto”) (78.6%), Skilled Venture LLC
(1.4%) and UKR Nexgen LLC (“UKR”) (20%). The members of Quinto will be Tryko Nexgen




                                                    1

===== PAGE 5 =====
Holdings LLC (“Tryko”) (72.26%) and RSBRMK Holdings LLC (“RSBRMK”) (27.74%). The
members of Tryko will be YR Nexgen Trust (50.002%), SK Nexgen Trust (24.999%) and YK Nexgen
Trust (24.999%). The members of RSBRMK will be NFR 2020 Irrevocable Trust (99.999%) and
Fraide Rokeach (.001%). The members of UKR will be UAK 2020 Irrevocable Trust (99.999%) and
Uri Kahanow (.001%). The pre and post Transaction organizational charts are at Tab 15.

The Applicant and its affiliates have a proven history of providing high-quality long-term care
services to their nursing facility residents. The nursing facility affiliates of the Applicant are third-
generation operators and own forty-one (41) skilled nursing facilities in seven (7) states: Maryland,
Massachusetts, New Jersey, Florida, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania and Virginia. The Applicant’s
affiliate is currently the licensed operator of Lincolnwood Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center,
Elmhurst Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center, and Bayview Operator, LLC in North Kingstown,
Rhode Island. Several of the Applicant’s affiliated skilled nursing facilities have received four and
five-star ratings in U.S. New and World Reports “Best Nursing Homes” list.

The Applicant will be independently operated and managed by an experienced facility-employed
administrator. It maintains consulting agreements with Marquis Health Consulting Services
(“Marquis”) for assistance with administrative services such as policy and procedure development
and marking services; with Clinical Care Consulting (“Clinical Care”) for assistance with clinical
planning and strategy; and with Cedarbridge Financial Services (“Cedarbridge”) for assistance
with back office, billing, payroll and account receivable services. Neither Marquis, Clinical Care
nor Cedarbridge will serve in any capacity as operator or manager of the Applicant. They also do
not have any authority to hire or fire the Facility’s chief executive officer, maintain or control the
books and records of the Facility, dispose of assets or incur liabilities on behalf of the Facility, or
adopt or enforce policies regarding the operation of the Facility. Please see consulting agreements
attached at Tab 1.

All the facilities associated with the Applicant are in substantial compliance with the licensing
agencies in their respective states

any services that will be added, terminated, expanded, or reduced and state the reasons therefore:

Center.

religion, national origin, sex, gender, handicap, disability, blindness, source of sponsorship, source
of payment, marital status, age, sexual preference, genetic disposition, or carrier status in the

disability, blindness, source of sponsorship, source of payment, marital status, age, sexual

21. Please identify any planned actions of the applicant to reduce, limit, or contain health care costs and
improve the efficiency with which health care services are delivered to the citizens of this state.

The Applicant will implement clinically guided programs to reduce hospitalizations or unplanned
discharges by working closely with physicians and acute care partners. The Applicant will employ
specialized electronic medical records, as well as specialty clinical programs, along with telehealth
to help reduce healthcare costs. In addition, the Applicant will implement UrgentSNF for patients.
This provides an alternative option to individuals who do not meet acute admissions criteria but
require and/or will benefit from supervisory skilled nursing oversight or stabilization. These
services are provided at a discounted rate for up to 14 days. This rate is all inclusive of room/board,
meals, therapy and nursing services.

22. Please provide a copy of the Quality Assurance Policies (for the services) and a detailed explanation
of how quality assurance for patient services will be implemented at the facility/ies by the applicant.

The Applicant will maintain a robust Quality Assurance program. See Tab 22 for the Quality
Assurance Policies. As set forth therein the Quality Assurance program will ensure facility systems
and processes to support the delivery of quality care and services. It likewise will help to identify
actual and potential negative outcomes relative to resident care and resolve them appropriately.

23. Please provide a detailed description about the amount and source of the equity and debt commitment
for this transaction. (NOTE: If debt is contemplated as part of the financing, please complete Appendix E).
Additionally, please demonstrate the following:

   A. The immediate and long-term financial feasibility of the proposed financing plan;
      Funding for the acquisition totals $ 6,920,543.00. The Applicant anticipates it will fund the
      purchase price as follows: 1) $ 1,384,109.00 from the Applicant’s cash on hand, which will
      represent a 20% equity position and 2) $ 5,536,434.00 in the form of a loan, which is 80% of
      the purchase price. Based on the pro forma set forth in Appendix A, there is adequate
      revenue for the proposed financing plan. Further, the Applicant’s members and ultimate
      parents have the funds to support the Applicant if necessary as set forth in Tab 28.

   B. The relative availability of funds for capital and operating needs; and

       Please see above description of both the capital funds available through Applicant’s equity
       contribution and the loan. Additionally, as set forth in the Pro Forma and evidence of thirty-
       days (30) operating expenses in Appendix C, the Applicant and its parents have access to
       sufficient funds for all operating needs.

  C. The applicant’s financial capability.

       The Applicant is a newly formed entity and a wholly owned subsidiary of Qunito Nexgen,
       which was formed in 2021. The Applicant’s financial capacity is documented in the financial
       statements of Quinto Delta, a related entity, included at Tab 28. Quinto Delta’s asset portfolio
       includes both the operator and real estate components of five nursing facilities; the company is
       diversified not only across the facilities in terms of market locations, but also across operations
       and real property. The Quinto Delta income statement itemizes the patient mix across the five
       facilities and reflects the aggregate operating revenue and expense of the facilities from their
       respective date of acquisition. Quinto Delta’s balance sheet indicates a debt to equity ratio of
       1.0, showing unusual financial strength for a company that has undertaken five acquisitions in
       the last year. During this short period, Quinto Delta maintains annualized free cash flow of
       over $12.5 million for the five facilities. In terms of funding operating expenses of the
       Applicant the cash flow generated by Quinto Delta will provide an added cushion.

       As the 75.4 % owner of Quinto Delta, Tryko’s Delta’s financials (included at Tab 28) reflect its
       proportionate ownership of the same asset portfolio held by Quinto Delta. Neither Quinto
       Delta nor Tryko Delta hold assets other than the nursing facilities in the Quinto Delta
       portfolio.

                                           Appendix C (CONT.)

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational policies
and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a sense of
peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

           a. Resident’s physical environment:
                  i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                      Residents’ bedrooms allow for privacy. Private, single-occupancy rooms, as well
                      as semi-private rooms, provide space for private living. A privacy curtain and
                      individual closet and storage space allow for privacy in semi-private rooms.
                      Studio apartment settings are provided to short-term residents and hospice
                      residents. Each of the resident rooms is equipped with Wi-Fi, cable television,
                      and telephones. The common center includes an on-site beauty salon, computer
                      facility, fitness area, and common rooms that allow for communal activities and
                      social gatherings with friends and family. Activities and space utilization is
                      guided by a certified activities director.

                  ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                      Residents may furnish their rooms with their own furniture or may use furniture
                      provided by the facility. If residents provide their own furniture, it must conform
                      to the extent that space and fire safety allow.

                  iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s),
                       laundry, activities;

                      The facility houses several kitchenettes for resident and family use that are
                      conveniently located within each resident neighborhood.

                  iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
                      gardening);

                      Residents may enjoy being outdoors independently and in organized activities.
                      The facilities include outdoor common areas and patios for cookouts and other
                      social gatherings.

           b. Resident-centered systems of care:

                   i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and negotiated
                      risk;

                      The facility protects its residents by utilizing a security system that prevents
                      those at risk from exiting the facility without staff oversight. This ensures that at-
                      risk residents remain safe, while also permitting autonomous residents to exit the




                                                     19

===== PAGE 23 =====
          facility. The facility also houses a CCTV system in the common areas and exits to
          ensure that the premises always remain safe and secure. Furthermore, residents
          have access to a call system that instantly notifies the staff via pagers when there
          is a need for immediate assistance.

      ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

          Skilled physicians determine the needed care of patients on a person-to-person
          basis through daily medical observation and guidance with daily activities. This
          individualized care includes the development of daily programs for walking,
          exercising, and group activities. If a resident is unable to provide their
          individualized preferences, physicians will communicate with the resident’s
          family members to determine an appropriate care plan. Specifically, the
          physicians will review the information, discuss the patient’s background with one
          another, and update the care plan accordingly.

      iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

          The facility provides daily menus that offer regular meals and specialty dishes.
          The kitchen staff can alter these dishes to comply with a resident’s dietary
          restrictions or personal preferences. If a resident cannot communicate their
          dietary restrictions or preferences, the facility will reach out to the resident’s
          family to serve the appropriate meals. Information regarding dietary restrictions
          and preferences is included in the resident care plans, reviewed with each care
          plan meeting, and updated accordingly. Additionally, residents have the option
          to dine in their rooms or in common areas, and their preference of setting may
          vary with each meal. The facility encourages residents to participate in the
          development of the menu items, especially during the holiday seasons.

      iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

          The facility provides residents with individualized recreation programs based on
          their personal preferences and needs. Activities include arts and crafts, movie
          screenings, exercise activities, musical entertainment, religious services, and
          cookouts in the summer.

c. Workforce administration:

       i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident
          services and foster relationship building?

          Heritage Hills Center utilizes the Consistent Assignment model of care. This
          method produces a close relationship between the resident and caregiver by
          facilitating feelings of comfort and trust. This model of care is further supported
          by the Resident Life Stories program, which tells the life story of the resident to
          his or her caregiver. These life details help caregivers develop meaningful




                                              20

===== PAGE 24 =====
    relationships with their residents. Lastly, the Interact Stop and Watch program
    is most effective when staffing with Consistent Assignment and fall prevention,
    observation of weight loss, and maintenance of skin integrity are all more
    effective with Consistent Assignment.

ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g. Registered
    nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

    Heritage Hills Center maintains a robust employee retention program and a
    culture of recognition and respect. This strategy is the key to maintaining
    consistent care standards because it minimizes turnover. Ultimately, one of
    Heritage Hill Center’s greatest strengths is its longevity of its staff, which it hopes
    to maintain in the long term.

1.    Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited.

Morgan Operator LLC d/b/a Morgan Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center (“Morgan” or
“Applicant”) seeks approval for the acquisition of Morgan Health Center, a 91 bed licensed skilled
nursing facility located at 80 Morgan Avenue, Johnston, RI 02919 (the “Facility”). Pursuant to the
terms of 1) the Asset Purchase Agreement as amended on October 15, 2021 by and among Health
Concepts Ltd. (“Health Concepts”), Trinity Square, LLC, River View Nursing Home Inc. d/b/a
River View Health Care Community, Village House Convalescent Home, Inc. d/b/a Village Health
Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, Village House Convalescent Home Associates LLC, Elmwood
Health Center, Inc. d/b/a Elmwood Health Center, David M. Ryan, Sally J. Ryan, Elmwood Avenue
Realty LLC, Ryan Health Center Inc. d/b/a Morgan Health Center, 76 Morgan, LLC, Westerly
Health Center Associates Limited Partnership d/b/a Westerly Health Center, Burrillville Health
Center Associates Limited Partnership d/b/a Bayberry Commons, Warwick Health Centre, Inc.
d/b/a West Shore Health Center, Wellshore Properties, LLC, Allen’s Health Center Inc. d/b/a
South Kingstown Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, 80 Douglas Pike LLC d/b/a Heritage Hills
Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, 198 Waterman Avenue LLC d/b/a Eastgate Nursing &
Rehabilitation Center, Ryan Finance, LLC (collectively, the “Sellers”) and RSO Investments, LLC
(the “Buyer”), 2) an Operations Transfer Agreement made and entered on the July 8, 2021 by and
between 80 Douglas Pike LLC (“Old Operator”) and Shore Point Holdings, LLC, and 3) the
Membership Interest Purchase Agreement by and between Rainwood Holdings LLC, Bayberry
Rehabilitation & Nursing LLC, RSO Investments LLC, Garden Property Holdings LLC, Lakeland
Equities LLC, RSO Holdings LLC, Shore Point Equities LLC, Shore Point Investments LLC and
Brick Garden Equities LLC, (the “Proposed Transaction”) all of the Facility’s assets including its
real estate and operating assets will be conveyed to Morgan Health Center LLC (“Morgan
Property”) and Morgan, respectively. Morgan Property will enter into a lease agreement with
Morgan. A copy of the Proposed Transaction agreements and lease are attached at Tabs 14 and 24,
respectively. As part of the Proposed Transaction, the Applicant and its affiliates seek to acquire a
total of four Rhode Island facilities (and are filing four CEC Applications) all currently owned and
operated by Health Concepts entities:

- Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center
- Morgan Health Center
- Riverview Healthcare Community
- Westerly Health Center

The total purchase price allocation for the acquisition of the operations and real estate of the
Facility is $8,304,651.16. The Applicant anticipates it will fund the purchase price as follows: 1)
$1,660,930.00 from the Applicant’s cash on hand, which will represent a 20% equity position and 2)
$6,643,721.00 in the form of a loan, which will represent an 80% debt position.

The Applicant is wholly owned by Quinto Nexgen LLC (“Quinto”) (78.6%), Skilled Venture LLC
(1.4%) and UKR Nexgen LLC (“UKR”) (20%). The members of Quinto will be Tryko Nexgen
Holdings LLC (“Tryko”) (72.26%) and RSBRMK Holdings LLC (“RSBRMK”) (27.74%). The

members of Tryko will be YR Nexgen Trust (50.002%), SK Nexgen Trust (24.999%) and YK Nexgen

The Applicant and its affiliates have a proven history of providing high-quality long-term care
services to their nursing facility residents. The nursing facility affiliates of the Applicant are third-
generation operators and own forty-one (41) skilled nursing facilities in seven (7) states: Maryland,
Massachusetts, New Jersey, Florida, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania and Virginia. The Applicant’s
affiliate is currently the licensed operator of Lincolnwood Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center,
Elmhurst Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center, and Bayview Operator, LLC in North Kingstown,
Rhode Island. Several of the Applicant’s affiliated skilled nursing facilities have received four and
five-star ratings in U.S. New and World Reports “Best Nursing Homes” list.

The Applicant will be independently operated and managed by an experienced facility-employed
administrator. It maintains consulting agreements with Marquis Health Consulting Services
(“Marquis”) for assistance with administrative services such as policy and procedure development
and marking services; with Clinical Care Consulting (“Clinical Care”) for assistance with clinical
planning and strategy; and with Cedarbridge Financial Services (“Cedarbridge”) for assistance
with back office, billing, payroll and account receivable services. Neither Marquis, Clinical Care
nor Cedarbridge will serve in any capacity as operator or manager the Applicant. They also do not
have any authority to hire or fire the Facility’s chief executive officer, maintain or control the books
and records of the Facility, dispose of assets or incur liabilities on behalf of the Facility, or adopt or
enforce policies regarding the operation of the Facility. Please see consulting agreements attached
at Tab 1.

All the facilities associated with the Applicant are in substantial compliance with the licensing
agencies in their respective states

21. Please identify any planned actions of the applicant to reduce, limit, or contain health care costs and
improve the efficiency with which health care services are delivered to the citizens of this state.

The Applicant will implement clinically guided programs to reduce hospitalizations or unplanned
discharges by working closely with physicians and acute care partners. The Applicant will employ
specialized electronic medical records, as well as specialty clinical programs, along with telehealth
to help reduce healthcare costs. In addition, the Applicant will implement UrgentSNF for patients.
This provides an alternative option to individuals who do not meet acute admissions criteria but
require and/or will benefit from supervisory skilled nursing oversight or stabilization. These
services are provided at a discounted rate for up to 14 days. This rate is all inclusive of room/board,
meals, therapy and nursing services.

  C. The applicant’s financial capability.

       The Applicant is a newly formed entity and a wholly owned subsidiary of Qunito Nexgen,
       which was formed in 2021. The Applicant’s financial capacity is documented in the financial
       statements of Quinto Delta, a related entity, included at Tab 28. Quinto Delta’s asset portfolio
       includes both the operator and real estate components of five nursing facilities; the company is
       diversified not only across the facilities in terms of market locations, but also across operations
       and real property. The Quinto Delta income statement itemizes the patient mix across the five
       facilities and reflects the aggregate operating revenue and expense of the facilities from their
       respective date of acquisition. Quinto Delta’s balance sheet indicates a debt to equity ratio of
       1.0, showing unusual financial strength for a company that has undertaken five acquisitions in
       the last year. During this short period, Quinto Delta maintains annualized free cash flow of
       over $12.5 million for the five facilities. In terms of funding operating expenses of the
       Applicant the cash flow generated by Quinto Delta will provide an added cushion.

       As the 75.4 % owner of Quinto Delta, Tryko’s Delta’s financials (included at Tab 28) reflect its
       proportionate ownership of the same asset portfolio held by Quinto Delta. Neither Quinto
       Delta nor Tryko Delta hold assets other than the nursing facilities in the Quinto Delta
       portfolio.

                                         Appendix C (CONT.)

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

           a. Resident’s physical environment:
                  i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                      Residents’ bedrooms allow for privacy. Private, single-occupancy rooms, as
                      well as semi-private rooms, provide space for private living. A privacy curtain
                      and individual closet and storage space allow for privacy in semi-private
                      rooms. Studio apartment settings are provided to short-term residents and
                      hospice residents. Each of the resident rooms is equipped with Wi-Fi, cable
                      television, and telephones. The common center includes an on-site beauty
                      salon, computer facility, fitness area, and common rooms that allow for
                      communal activities and social gatherings with friends and family. Activities
                      and space utilization is guided by a certified activities director.

                  ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                      Residents may furnish their rooms with their own furniture or may use
                      furniture provided by the facility. If residents provide their own furniture, it
                      must conform to the extent that space and fire safety allow.

                 iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s),
                      laundry, activities;

                      The facility houses several kitchenettes for resident and family use that are
                      conveniently located within each resident neighborhood.

                 iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
                     gardening);

                      Residents may enjoy being outdoors independently and in organized activities.
                      The facilities include outdoor common areas and patios for cookouts and other
                      social gatherings.

           b. Resident-centered systems of care:

                   i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and
                      negotiated risk;

                      The facility protects its residents by utilizing a security system that prevents
                      those at risk from exiting the facility without staff oversight. This ensures that
                      at-risk residents remain safe, while also permitting autonomous residents to




                                                   19

===== PAGE 53 =====
          exit the facility. The facility also houses a CCTV system in the common areas
          and exits to ensure that the premises always remain safe and secure.
          Furthermore, residents have access to a call system that instantly notifies the
          staff via pagers when there is a need for immediate assistance.

      ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

          Skilled physicians determine the needed care of patients on a person-to-person
          basis through daily medical observation and guidance with daily activities.
          This individualized care includes the development of daily programs for
          walking, exercising, and group activities. If a resident is unable to provide
          their individualized preferences, physicians will communicate with the
          resident’s family members to determine an appropriate care plan.
          Specifically, the physicians will review the information, discuss the patient’s
          background with one another, and update the care plan accordingly.

      iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

          The facility provides daily menus that offer regular meals and specialty dishes.
          The kitchen staff can alter these dishes to comply with a resident’s dietary
          restrictions or personal preferences. If a resident cannot communicate their
          dietary restrictions or preferences, the facility will reach out to the resident’s
          family to serve the appropriate meals. Information regarding dietary
          restrictions and preferences is included in the resident care plans, reviewed
          with each care plan meeting, and updated accordingly. Additionally, residents
          have the option to dine in their rooms or in common areas, and their
          preference of setting may vary with each meal. The facility encourages
          residents to participate in the development of the menu items, especially
          during the holiday seasons.

      iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

          The facility provides residents with individualized recreation programs based
          on their personal preferences and needs. Activities include arts and crafts,
          movie screenings, exercise activities, musical entertainment, religious services,
          and cookouts in the summer.

c. Workforce administration:

       i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident
          services and foster relationship building?

          The Facility utilizes the Consistent Assignment model of care. This method
          produces a close relationship between the resident and caregiver by
          facilitating feelings of comfort and trust. This model of care is further
          supported by the Resident Life Stories program, which tells the life story of




                                          20

===== PAGE 54 =====
   the resident to his or her caregiver. These life details help caregivers develop
   meaningful relationships with their residents. Lastly, the Interact Stop and
   Watch program is most effective when staffing with Consistent Assignment
   and fall prevention, observation of weight loss, and maintenance of skin
   integrity are all more effective with Consistent Assignment.

ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g.
    Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

   The Facility maintains a robust employee retention program and a culture of
   recognition and respect. This strategy is the key to maintaining consistent
   care standards because it minimizes turnover. Ultimately, one of the Facility’s
   greatest strengths is its longevity of its staff, which it hopes to maintain in the
   long term.

1.    Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and

applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited.

Riverview Operator LLC d/b/a Riverview Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center (“Riverview” or
“Applicant”) seeks approval for the acquisition of Riverview Healthcare Community, a 190 bed
licensed skilled nursing facility located at 546 Main Street Coventry, RI 02816 (the “Facility”).
Pursuant to the terms of 1) the Asset Purchase Agreement as amended on October 15, 2021 by and
among Health Concepts Ltd. (“Health Concepts”), Trinity Square, LLC, River View Nursing Home
Inc. d/b/a River View Health Care Community, Village House Convalescent Home, Inc. d/b/a
Village Health Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, Village House Convalescent Home Associates
LLC, Elmwood Health Center, Inc. d/b/a Elmwood Health Center, David M. Ryan, Sally J. Ryan,
Elmwood Avenue Realty LLC, Ryan Health Center Inc. d/b/a Morgan Health Center, 76 Morgan,
LLC, Westerly Health Center Associates Limited Partnership d/b/a Westerly Health Center,
Burrillville Health Center Associates Limited Partnership d/b/a Bayberry Commons, Warwick
Health Centre, Inc. d/b/a West Shore Health Center, Wellshore Properties, LLC, Allen’s Health
Center Inc. d/b/a South Kingstown Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, 80 Douglas Pike LLC d/b/a
Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, 198 Waterman Avenue LLC d/b/a Eastgate
Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, Ryan Finance, LLC (collectively, the “Sellers”) and RSO
Investments, LLC (the “Buyer”), 2) an Operations Transfer Agreement made and entered on the
July 8, 2021 by and between 80 Douglas Pike LLC (“Old Operator”) and Shore Point Holdings,
LLC, and 3) the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement by and between Rainwood Holdings
LLC, Bayberry Rehabilitation & Nursing LLC, RSO Investments LLC, Garden Property Holdings
LLC, Lakeland Equities LLC, RSO Holdings LLC, Shore Point Equities LLC, Shore Point
Investments LLC and Brick Garden Equities LLC, (“the Proposed Transaction”) all of the
Facility’s assets including its real estate and operating assets will be conveyed to Riverview
Property LLC (“Riverview Property”) and Riverview, respectively. Riverview Property will enter
into a lease agreement with Riverview. A copy of the Proposed Transaction agreements and lease
are attached at Tabs 14 and 24, respectively. As part of the Proposed Transaction, the Applicant
and its affiliates seek to acquire a total of four Rhode Island facilities (and are filing four CEC
Applications) all currently owned and operated by Health Concepts entities:

- Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center
- Morgan Health Center
- Riverview Healthcare Community
- Westerly Health Center

The total purchase price allocation for the acquisition of the operations and real estate of the
Facility is $13,149,031.01. The Applicant anticipates it will fund the purchase price as follows: 1)
$2,629,806.00 from the Applicant’s cash on hand, which will represent a 20% equity position and 2)

21. Please identify any planned actions of the applicant to reduce, limit, or contain health care costs and
improve the efficiency with which health care services are delivered to the citizens of this state.

The Applicant will implement clinically guided programs to reduce hospitalizations or unplanned
discharges by working closely with physicians and acute care partners. The Applicant will employ
specialized electronic medical records, as well as specialty clinical programs, along with telehealth
to help reduce healthcare costs. In addition, the Applicant will implement UrgentSNF for patients.
This provides an alternative option to individuals who do not meet acute admissions criteria but
require and/or will benefit from supervisory skilled nursing oversight or stabilization. These
services are provided at a discounted rate for up to 14 days. This rate is all inclusive of room/board,
meals, therapy and nursing services.

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

           a. Resident’s physical environment:
                  i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                      Residents’ bedrooms allow for privacy. Private, single-occupancy rooms, as
                      well as semi-private rooms, provide space for private living. A privacy curtain
                      and individual closet and storage space allow for privacy in semi-private
                      rooms. Studio apartment settings are provided to short-term residents and
                      hospice residents. Each of the resident rooms is equipped with Wi-Fi, cable
                      television, and telephones. The common center includes an on-site beauty
                      salon, computer facility, fitness area, and common rooms that allow for
                      communal activities and social gatherings with friends and family. Activities
                      and space utilization is guided by a certified activities director.

                  ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                      Residents may furnish their rooms with their own furniture or may use
                      furniture provided by the facility. If residents provide their own furniture, it
                      must conform to the extent that space and fire safety allow.

                 iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s),
                      laundry, activities;

                      The facility houses several kitchenettes for resident and family use that are
                      conveniently located within each resident neighborhood.

                 iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
                     gardening);

                      Residents may enjoy being outdoors independently and in organized activities.
                      The facilities include outdoor common areas and patios for cookouts and other
                      social gatherings.

           b. Resident-centered systems of care:

                   i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and
                      negotiated risk;

                      The facility protects its residents by utilizing a security system that prevents
                      those at risk from exiting the facility without staff oversight. This ensures that
                      at-risk residents remain safe, while also permitting autonomous residents to




                                                   19

===== PAGE 83 =====
          exit the facility. The facility also houses a CCTV system in the common areas
          and exits to ensure that the premises always remain safe and secure.
          Furthermore, residents have access to a call system that instantly notifies the
          staff via pagers when there is a need for immediate assistance.

      ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

          Skilled physicians determine the needed care of patients on a person-to-person
          basis through daily medical observation and guidance with daily activities.
          This individualized care includes the development of daily programs for
          walking, exercising, and group activities. If a resident is unable to provide
          their individualized preferences, physicians will communicate with the
          resident’s family members to determine an appropriate care plan.
          Specifically, the physicians will review the information, discuss the patient’s
          background with one another, and update the care plan accordingly.

      iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

          The facility provides daily menus that offer regular meals and specialty dishes.
          The kitchen staff can alter these dishes to comply with a resident’s dietary
          restrictions or personal preferences. If a resident cannot communicate their
          dietary restrictions or preferences, the facility will reach out to the resident’s
          family to serve the appropriate meals. Information regarding dietary
          restrictions and preferences is included in the resident care plans, reviewed
          with each care plan meeting, and updated accordingly. Additionally, residents
          have the option to dine in their rooms or in common areas, and their
          preference of setting may vary with each meal. The facility encourages
          residents to participate in the development of the menu items, especially
          during the holiday seasons.

      iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

          The facility provides residents with individualized recreation programs based
          on their personal preferences and needs. Activities include arts and crafts,
          movie screenings, exercise activities, musical entertainment, religious services,
          and cookouts in the summer.

c. Workforce administration:

       i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident
          services and foster relationship building?

          The Facility utilizes the Consistent Assignment model of care. This method
          produces a close relationship between the resident and caregiver by
          facilitating feelings of comfort and trust. This model of care is further
          supported by the Resident Life Stories program, which tells the life story of




                                          20

===== PAGE 84 =====
   the resident to his or her caregiver. These life details help caregivers develop
   meaningful relationships with their residents. Lastly, the Interact Stop and
   Watch program is most effective when staffing with Consistent Assignment
   and fall prevention, observation of weight loss, and maintenance of skin
   integrity are all more effective with Consistent Assignment.

ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g.
    Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

   The Facility maintains a robust employee retention program and a culture of
   recognition and respect. This strategy is the key to maintaining consistent
   care standards because it minimizes turnover. Ultimately, one of the Facility’s
   greatest strengths is its longevity of its staff, which it hopes to maintain in the
   long term.

Rehabilitation & Nursing LLC, RSO Investments LLC, Garden Property Holdings LLC, Lakeland

21. Please identify any planned actions of the applicant to reduce, limit, or contain health care costs and
improve the efficiency with which health care services are delivered to the citizens of this state.

The Applicant will implement clinically guided programs to reduce hospitalizations or unplanned
discharges by working closely with physicians and acute care partners. The Applicant will employ
specialized electronic medical records, as well as specialty clinical programs, along with telehealth
to help reduce healthcare costs. In addition, the Applicant will implement UrgentSNF for patients.
This provides an alternative option to individuals who do not meet acute admissions criteria but
require and/or will benefit from supervisory skilled nursing oversight or stabilization. These
services are provided at a discounted rate for up to 14 days. This rate is all inclusive of room/board,
meals, therapy and nursing services.

       statements of Quinto Delta, a related entity, included at Tab 28. Quinto Delta’s asset portfolio
       includes both the operator and real estate components of five nursing facilities; the company is
       diversified not only across the facilities in terms of market locations, but also across operations

       respective date of acquisition. Quinto Delta’s balance sheet indicates a debt to equity ratio of

                                         Appendix C (CONT.)

5.      Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and operational
policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services, and accommodations, and a
sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the proposal would advance these areas:

           a. Resident’s physical environment:
                  i. Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                      Residents’ bedrooms allow for privacy. Private, single-occupancy rooms, as
                      well as semi-private rooms, provide space for private living. A privacy curtain
                      and individual closet and storage space allow for privacy in semi-private
                      rooms. Studio apartment settings are provided to short-term residents and
                      hospice residents. Each of the resident rooms is equipped with Wi-Fi, cable
                      television, and telephones. The common center includes an on-site beauty
                      salon, computer facility, fitness area, and common rooms that allow for
                      communal activities and social gatherings with friends and family. Activities
                      and space utilization is guided by a certified activities director.

                  ii. Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                      Residents may furnish their rooms with their own furniture or may use
                      furniture provided by the facility. If residents provide their own furniture, it
                      must conform to the extent that space and fire safety allow.

                 iii. Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community kitchen(s),
                      laundry, activities;

                      The facility houses several kitchenettes for resident and family use that are
                      conveniently located within each resident neighborhood.

                 iv. Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens and
                     gardening);

                      Residents may enjoy being outdoors independently and in organized activities.
                      The facilities include outdoor common areas and patios for cookouts and other
                      social gatherings.

           b. Resident-centered systems of care:

                   i. Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and
                      negotiated risk;

                      The facility protects its residents by utilizing a security system that prevents
                      those at risk from exiting the facility without staff oversight. This ensures that
                      at-risk residents remain safe, while also permitting autonomous residents to




                                                   19

===== PAGE 113 =====
          exit the facility. The facility also houses a CCTV system in the common areas
          and exits to ensure that the premises always remain safe and secure.
          Furthermore, residents have access to a call system that instantly notifies the
          staff via pagers when there is a need for immediate assistance.

      ii. Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed, waking);

          Skilled physicians determine the needed care of patients on a person-to-person
          basis through daily medical observation and guidance with daily activities.
          This individualized care includes the development of daily programs for
          walking, exercising, and group activities. If a resident is unable to provide
          their individualized preferences, physicians will communicate with the
          resident’s family members to determine an appropriate care plan.
          Specifically, the physicians will review the information, discuss the patient’s
          background with one another, and update the care plan accordingly.

      iii. Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

          The facility provides daily menus that offer regular meals and specialty dishes.
          The kitchen staff can alter these dishes to comply with a resident’s dietary
          restrictions or personal preferences. If a resident cannot communicate their
          dietary restrictions or preferences, the facility will reach out to the resident’s
          family to serve the appropriate meals. Information regarding dietary
          restrictions and preferences is included in the resident care plans, reviewed
          with each care plan meeting, and updated accordingly. Additionally, residents
          have the option to dine in their rooms or in common areas, and their
          preference of setting may vary with each meal. The facility encourages
          residents to participate in the development of the menu items, especially
          during the holiday seasons.

      iv. Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

          The facility provides residents with individualized recreation programs based
          on their personal preferences and needs. Activities include arts and crafts,
          movie screenings, exercise activities, musical entertainment, religious services,
          and cookouts in the summer.

c. Workforce administration:

       i. How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of resident
          services and foster relationship building?

          The Facility utilizes the Consistent Assignment model of care. This method
          produces a close relationship between the resident and caregiver by
          facilitating feelings of comfort and trust. This model of care is further
          supported by the Resident Life Stories program, which tells the life story of




                                          20

===== PAGE 114 =====
   the resident to his or her caregiver. These life details help caregivers develop
   meaningful relationships with their residents. Lastly, the Interact Stop and
   Watch program is most effective when staffing with Consistent Assignment
   and fall prevention, observation of weight loss, and maintenance of skin
   integrity are all more effective with Consistent Assignment.

ii. Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g.
    Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

   The Facility maintains a robust employee retention program and a culture of
   recognition and respect. This strategy is the key to maintaining consistent
   care standards because it minimizes turnover. Ultimately, one of the Facility’s
   greatest strengths is its longevity of its staff, which it hopes to maintain in the
   long term.

                         CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT

      THIS SERVICES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of this
___ day of ___________, 202_ (the “Effective Date”) by and between HERITAGE HILLS
OPERATOR LLC (“Licensee”), as licensed operator, and CEDARBRIDGE FINANCIAL
SERVICES LLC (“Cedarbridge Service Consultant”).

                                           RECITALS

       WHEREAS, Licensee is the operator of a healthcare and rehabilitation facility located at
80 Douglas Pike, Smithfield, RI 02917 , to be known as Heriatge Hills Rehabilitation and
Healthcare Center (the “Facility”).

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant is engaged in the business of providing
financial services to long term care facilities with Licensee being solely responsible for the
operation of the Facility in compliance with applicable law;

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant has agreed to provide Services (as defined
in Section 2 hereof) to Licensee upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth;
with Licensee being solely responsible for the operation of the Facility in compliance with
applicable law and

Agreement and Licensee hereby retains Cedarbridge Service Consultant on and subject to the
terms, conditions and provisions set forth herein.

promises, which the parties set forth below, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt
and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

       operating at the Facility and shall continue until either party sends prior written notice to
       the other party of that party’s intent to terminate this Agreement sixty (60) days prior to
       the annual anniversary of the Effective Date unless the Term is sooner terminated pursuant
       to the terms of the Agreement.

       THIS SERVICES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of this
___ day of ___________, 202_ (the “Effective Date”) by and between MORGAN OPERATOR
LLC (“Licensee”), as licensed operator, and CEDARBRIDGE FINANCIAL SERVICES LLC
(“Cedarbridge Service Consultant”).

                                           RECITALS

       WHEREAS, Licensee is the operator of a healthcare and rehabilitation facility located at
80 Morgan Avenue, Johnston, RI 02919 , to be known as Morgan Rehabilitation and Healthcare
Center (the “Facility”).

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant is engaged in the business of providing
financial services to long term care facilities with Licensee being solely responsible for the
operation of the Facility in compliance with applicable law;

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant has agreed to provide Services (as defined
in Section 2 hereof) to Licensee upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth;
with Licensee being solely responsible for the operation of the Facility in compliance with
applicable law and

        WHEREAS, Licensee and Cedarbridge Service Consultant have agreed to enter into this
Agreement and Licensee hereby retains Cedarbridge Service Consultant on and subject to the
terms, conditions and provisions set forth herein.

       NOW THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements and
promises, which the parties set forth below, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt
and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

1.     Term. The term of this Agreement (“Term”) shall commence when the Licensee begins
       operating at the Facility and shall continue until either party sends prior written notice to
       the other party of that party’s intent to terminate this Agreement sixty (60) days prior to
       the annual anniversary of the Effective Date unless the Term is sooner terminated pursuant
       to the terms of the Agreement.

2.     Duties. Cedarbridge Service Consultant shall perform the following services (the
       “Services”):

       (a)     Provide, in coordination with Licensee’s office staff, bookkeeping, accounting and
               reporting services for the Facility pertaining to all of its accounts receivable
               (including without limitation all private pay residents, Medicare residents, and
               Medicaid residents) and accounts payable, including but not limited to, routine
               billing of its accounts and assisting in the regular or periodic performance of the
               Facility’s cash flow analysis;

===== PAGE 142 =====
(b)   When necessary, at Licensee’s cost, secure the services of additional bookkeepers
      and contract accountants to prepare and review the Facility’s financial records and
      consult with and advise the Licensee and its agents regarding their timely
      preparation, content and submittals;

(c)   Assist with and provide for the timely preparing and filing of any and all financial
      records and/or reports (including but not limited to Medicaid and/or Medicare cost
      reports) relating to the Facility’s operation, and also financial plans to be reviewed
      and approved by Licensee on a periodic basis, including but not limited to: (a) an
      estimated profit and loss statement, in reasonable detail, for the current operating
      year; and (b) estimates for such operating year, covering expenditures for: (i)
      repairs and maintenance; (ii) the purchase of operating equipment; (iii) the purchase
      of furnishings and equipment; (iv) capital improvements; and (v) advertising and
      business promotion costs of the Facility;

(d)   Provide for the retention of and the appropriate monitoring of independent
      accountants and attorneys to timely prepare and file any and all required state and
      federal tax returns, appeals, etc.;

(e)   Perform on behalf of the Facility and jointly with the other facilities with whom
      Cedarbridge Service Consultant contracts from time to time, group purchasing and
      procurement of medical equipment, appliances, supplies, food and other items, as
      directed by the Licensee;

(f)   Provide or arrange with third parties, at Licensee’s cost, to provide all payroll
      functions including all regulatory and tax reporting functions relating to payroll
      administration.

(g)   Assist Licensee in establishing and maintaining banking relationships, including
      securing loans on behalf of Licensee, complying with the loan terms, supplying

      needs, to the extent of Licensee’s cash availability. As part of its cash management

                         CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT

      THIS SERVICES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of this
___ day of ___________, 202_ (the “Effective Date”) by and between RIVERVIEW
OPERATOR LLC (“Licensee”), as licensed operator, and CEDARBRIDGE FINANCIAL
SERVICES LLC (“Cedarbridge Service Consultant”).

                                           RECITALS

       WHEREAS, Licensee is the operator of a healthcare and rehabilitation facility located at
546 Main Street,Coventry, RI 02816 , to be known as Riverview Rehabilitation and Healthcare
Center (the “Facility”).

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant is engaged in the business of providing
financial services to long term care facilities with Licensee being solely responsible for the
operation of the Facility in compliance with applicable law;

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant has agreed to provide Services (as defined
in Section 2 hereof) to Licensee upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth;
with Licensee being solely responsible for the operation of the Facility in compliance with
applicable law and

        WHEREAS, Licensee and Cedarbridge Service Consultant have agreed to enter into this
Agreement and Licensee hereby retains Cedarbridge Service Consultant on and subject to the
terms, conditions and provisions set forth herein.

                                         AGREEMENT

       NOW THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements and
promises, which the parties set forth below, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt
and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

1.     Term. The term of this Agreement (“Term”) shall commence when the Licensee begins
       operating at the Facility and shall continue until either party sends prior written notice to
       the other party of that party’s intent to terminate this Agreement sixty (60) days prior to
       the annual anniversary of the Effective Date unless the Term is sooner terminated pursuant
       to the terms of the Agreement.

2.     Duties. Cedarbridge Service Consultant shall perform the following services (the
       “Services”):

       (a)     Provide, in coordination with Licensee’s office staff, bookkeeping, accounting and
               reporting services for the Facility pertaining to all of its accounts receivable
               (including without limitation all private pay residents, Medicare residents, and
               Medicaid residents) and accounts payable, including but not limited to, routine
               billing of its accounts and assisting in the regular or periodic performance of the
               Facility’s cash flow analysis;

===== PAGE 158 =====
(b)   When necessary, at Licensee’s cost, secure the services of additional bookkeepers
      and contract accountants to prepare and review the Facility’s financial records and
      consult with and advise the Licensee and its agents regarding their timely
      preparation, content and submittals;

(c)   Assist with and provide for the timely preparing and filing of any and all financial
      records and/or reports (including but not limited to Medicaid and/or Medicare cost
      reports) relating to the Facility’s operation, and also financial plans to be reviewed
      and approved by Licensee on a periodic basis, including but not limited to: (a) an
      estimated profit and loss statement, in reasonable detail, for the current operating
      year; and (b) estimates for such operating year, covering expenditures for: (i)
      repairs and maintenance; (ii) the purchase of operating equipment; (iii) the purchase
      of furnishings and equipment; (iv) capital improvements; and (v) advertising and
      business promotion costs of the Facility;

(d)   Provide for the retention of and the appropriate monitoring of independent
      accountants and attorneys to timely prepare and file any and all required state and
      federal tax returns, appeals, etc.;

(e)   Perform on behalf of the Facility and jointly with the other facilities with whom
      Cedarbridge Service Consultant contracts from time to time, group purchasing and
      procurement of medical equipment, appliances, supplies, food and other items, as

                         CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENT

       THIS SERVICES AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of this
___ day of ___________, 202_ (the “Effective Date”) by and between WESTERLY OPERATOR
LLC (“Licensee”), as licensed operator, and CEDARBRIDGE FINANCIAL SERVICES LLC
(“Cedarbridge Service Consultant”).

                                           RECITALS

       WHEREAS, Licensee is the operator of a healthcare and rehabilitation facility located at
280 High Street, Westerly, RI, 02891 , to be known as Westerly Rehabilitation and Healthcare
Center (the “Facility”).

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant is engaged in the business of providing
financial services to long term care facilities with Licensee being solely responsible for the
operation of the Facility in compliance with applicable law;

        WHEREAS, Cedarbridge Service Consultant has agreed to provide Services (as defined
in Section 2 hereof) to Licensee upon the terms and subject to the conditions hereinafter set forth;
with Licensee being solely responsible for the operation of the Facility in compliance with
applicable law and

        WHEREAS, Licensee and Cedarbridge Service Consultant have agreed to enter into this
Agreement and Licensee hereby retains Cedarbridge Service Consultant on and subject to the
terms, conditions and provisions set forth herein.

                                         AGREEMENT

       NOW THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements and
promises, which the parties set forth below, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt
and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

1.     Term. The term of this Agreement (“Term”) shall commence when the Licensee begins
       operating at the Facility and shall continue until either party sends prior written notice to
       the other party of that party’s intent to terminate this Agreement sixty (60) days prior to
       the annual anniversary of the Effective Date unless the Term is sooner terminated pursuant
       to the terms of the Agreement.

2.     Duties. Cedarbridge Service Consultant shall perform the following services (the
       “Services”):

       (a)     Provide, in coordination with Licensee’s office staff, bookkeeping, accounting and
               reporting services for the Facility pertaining to all of its accounts receivable
               (including without limitation all private pay residents, Medicare residents, and
               Medicaid residents) and accounts payable, including but not limited to, routine
               billing of its accounts and assisting in the regular or periodic performance of the
               Facility’s cash flow analysis;

===== PAGE 174 =====
(b)   When necessary, at Licensee’s cost, secure the services of additional bookkeepers
      and contract accountants to prepare and review the Facility’s financial records and
      consult with and advise the Licensee and its agents regarding their timely
      preparation, content and submittals;

(c)   Assist with and provide for the timely preparing and filing of any and all financial
      records and/or reports (including but not limited to Medicaid and/or Medicare cost
      reports) relating to the Facility’s operation, and also financial plans to be reviewed
      and approved by Licensee on a periodic basis, including but not limited to: (a) an
      estimated profit and loss statement, in reasonable detail, for the current operating
      year; and (b) estimates for such operating year, covering expenditures for: (i)
      repairs and maintenance; (ii) the purchase of operating equipment; (iii) the purchase
      of furnishings and equipment; (iv) capital improvements; and (v) advertising and
      business promotion costs of the Facility;

(d)   Provide for the retention of and the appropriate monitoring of independent
      accountants and attorneys to timely prepare and file any and all required state and
      federal tax returns, appeals, etc.;

(e)   Perform on behalf of the Facility and jointly with the other facilities with whom
      Cedarbridge Service Consultant contracts from time to time, group purchasing and
      procurement of medical equipment, appliances, supplies, food and other items, as
      directed by the Licensee;

(f)   Provide or arrange with third parties, at Licensee’s cost, to provide all payroll
      functions including all regulatory and tax reporting functions relating to payroll
      administration.

(g)   Assist Licensee in establishing and maintaining banking relationships, including
      securing loans on behalf of Licensee, complying with the loan terms, supplying
      banks with any and all necessary documentation to properly document and support
      loan levels and otherwise manage Licensee’s cash flow and cash management
      needs, to the extent of Licensee’s cash availability. As part of its cash management
      services, Cedarbridge Service Consultant may, with the consent of Licensee and
      other facilities, arrange for and process loans between Licensee and its affiliates in
      a manner that minimizes the interest and financing costs to Licensee and allows for
      the orderly cash management of funds for Licensee. Cedarbridge Service
      Consultant shall properly document any such loans and shall implement same only
      with the written consent of Licensee and such other facilities. Nothing contained
      herein shall require Cedarbridge Service Consultant to advance any sums to or for
      the benefit of Licensee;

(h)   Establish bank accounts in Licensee’s name for the Facility at banking or other
      financial institution(s) reasonably acceptable to Licensee. The Cedarbridge Service
      Consultant shall deposit in such accounts all monies received in the name of
      Licensee from the operation of the Facility and will disburse the same for the
      purposes set forth in (k) below with signature authority over bank accounts to which

===== PAGE 175 =====
            governmental accounts receivable shall be deposited being vested solely in
            Licensee;

     (i)    From the accounts referred to in (j) above or from other monies of Licensee, pay
            on behalf of, and in the name of Licensee, such amounts and at such times as are
            required in connection with the leasing, operation, management or maintenance of
            the Facility;

     (j)    Cedarbridge Service Consultant is empowered by the Licensee and authorized to
            act as its agent to negotiate rates of reimbursement from any and all applicable
            governmental agencies and non-governmental entities, and shall provide all books,
            records, and other financial information or any related audits thereof;

     (k)    Cedarbridge Service Consultant may, assist the Licensee – or its billing agency to,
            institute any and all actions or proceedings to collect charges or other income due
            to the Facility and to identify and make refunds or submit corrected claims to third
            party payers and residents as required by applicable law or contract, disclosures
            relating to claims, responses to additional development requests, payer audits,
            recoupments including pursuing appeals therefrom, as provided however, Licensee
            is responsible for the submission of all claims for reimbursement including without
            limitation compliance with all conditions of participation, conditions of payment,
            medical necessity requirements, documentation requirements, coverage
            requirements, or other billing requirements.

     (l)    Assist Licensee in preparing, maintaining and updating Licensees licensing and
            provider enrollment and relating filings.

     (m)    Assist Licensee on the ongoing maintenance, development and improvement of the
            Information Technology system to appropriately oversee confidential Facility
            functions including banking, treasury, cash management, risk management,
            workers’ compensation, therapy services, payroll, insurance, data,
            patient/employee data, NJS transmissions, attorney-client work products, etc.;

     (n)    Retain outside legal counsel to perform all legal services for Licensee; and

     (o)    Cedarbridge Service Consultant will make itself available to assist, advise and
            perform such other duties as may reasonably be requested by Licensee.
