           12. Heter Iska. The undersigned members of the Company hereby declare and admit that all advances made
between themselves with respect to capital contributions, loans to the company, capital calls, or any other mortgages,
guarantees, preferred investments, or any other advances, that would violate any of the laws of Ribbis shall be structured
as an Iska investment subject to the following terms. In exchange for the monies advanced, the recipient/beneficiary shall
transfer to the investor a share (of equal value) in his assets as an Iska. In the event that no such investment exists, or if
the recipient participates in a more lucrative investment opportunity in the future, the recipient shall assign a share of that
investment to the investor. This investment shall be owned by the investing partner, and all profits, capital gains, or
losses shall be his sole responsibility. The recipient shall have complete authority to manage this investment on behalf of
the investor, in the manner deemed most beneficial to the investor. Any investment owned by the recipient may be used
to create this Iska, provided that the venture is Halachacly permissible. This Iska may only be collected from the assets of
the Company and the investor shall have no claim against the personal assets of any of the recipients, unless otherwise
specified in an agreement between the parties. The recipient shall receive five percent of the profits as compensation for
his services managing this Iska, and shall be liable for the monies as a watchman. The recipient must verify any claim of
loss through the testimony of two Halachacly acceptable witnesses in an Orthodox Jewish court of law. Any claim
regarding the amount of profits generated by the joint venture must be verified with a solemn oath, administered by an
Orthodox Jewish court of law. In addition, the investor may demand full access to all legal records, documents, financial
statements or receipts that the investor deems necessary to verify the claims of the recipient. In the event of a claim of
loss, the investor may demand a full and immediate payment of the remaining balance of this Iska. It is agreed that if the
recipient pays the amount equal to the principal, interest, penalties, default rates, preferred returns, membership dilution,
buyout rights, or other benefits called for by this Agreement, as per the payment schedule of this Agreement, as payment
for the investor's share of the principal and profits of the Iska investment, the investor shall waive his right to demand
verification of the results of the investment. Any additional profits shall belong solely to the recipient. Such payment
shall reflect a final settlement, and the recipient shall have no further claim for compensation, management or services
fees, unless specified to the contrary in other agreements executed between the parties. Any payments made that are not
justified by this Iska agreement shall reduce the principal balance of this Iska. However, any future payments made to
avoid providing the abovementioned verification, shall be increased to compensate for any discrepancy. This section
shall override any other section, even those that do not reference this section. Any mention of loans or interest shall be
interpreted as an Iska and to payments mentioned above. This declaration is legally binding and may be enforced in any
Jewish or civil court, even in the event that one of the parties was unaware of its existence. This agreement has been
executed in an effective manner and with a proper Kinyan, if required.

         13. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts which together shall constitute one fully
executed Agreement. This Agreement shall become effective upon the exchange of facsimile or emailed signatures. A
copy of any parties’ signature shall be the same as an original.

                                              Tax Provisions

1.   Special Allocations. The following special allocations shall be made in the following order:

              (a)       Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations Section
     1.704-2(f), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in Company
     Minimum Gain during any fiscal year, each Member shall be specially allocated items of Company income
     and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such
     Member's share of the net decrease in Company Minimum Gain, determined in accordance with
     Regulations Section 1.704-2(g). Allocations pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in proportion
     to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The items to be so
     allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections 1.704-2(f)(6) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This
     Section 1(a) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement in Regulations Section
     1.704-2(f) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (b)       Member Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations
     Section 1.704-2(i)(4), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in
     Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to a Member Nonrecourse Debt during any fiscal
     year, each Member who has a share of the Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to such
     Member Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(5), shall be
     specially allocated items of Company income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent
     fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Member's share of the net decrease in Member Nonrecourse Debt,
     determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4). Allocations pursuant to the previous
     sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member
     pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections
     1.704-2(i)(4) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This Section 1(b) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback
     requirement in Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

              (c)       Qualified Income Offset. In the event any Member unexpectedly receives any
     adjustments, allocations, or distributions described in Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), Section
     1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(5), or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(6), items of Company income and gain shall be
     specially allocated to such Member in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate, to the extent required
     by the Regulations, the deficit balance in the Capital Account of such Member as quickly as possible,
     provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(c) shall be made only if and to the extent that such
     Member would have an deficit balance in its Capital Account after all other allocations provided for in this
     Exhibit have been tentatively made as if this Section 1(c) were not in this Exhibit.

               (d)      Gross Income Allocation. In the event any Member has a deficit Capital Account at the
     end of any fiscal year that is in excess of the amount such Member is obligated to restore pursuant to the
     penultimate sentences of Regulations Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(5), such Member shall be
     specially allocated items of Company income and gain in the amount of such excess as quickly as possible,
     provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(d) shall be made only if and to the extent that such
     Member would have a deficit Capital Account in excess of such amount after all other allocations provided
     for in this Exhibit have been made as if Section 1(c) and this Section 1(d) were not in this Agreement.

              (e)        Nonrecourse Deductions. Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal year shall be specially
     allocated to all of the Members in proportion to the Membership Interests of the Members.

              (f)     Member Nonrecourse Deductions. Any Member Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal
     year shall be specially allocated to the Member who bears the economic risk of loss with respect to the
     Member Nonrecourse Debt to which such Member Nonrecourse Deductions are attributable in accordance
     with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(1).



                                                     12

===== PAGE 1171 =====
                   (g)      Section 754 Adjustments. To the extent an adjustment to the adjusted tax basis of any
         Company asset pursuant to Code Section 734(b) or Section 743(b) is required, pursuant to Regulations
         Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4), to be taken into account in determining
         Capital Accounts as the result of a distribution to a Member in complete liquidation of such Member's
         interest in the Company, the amount of such adjustment to the Capital Accounts shall be treated as an item
         of gain (if the adjustment increases the basis of the asset) or as an item of loss (if the adjustment decreases
         such basis), and such gain or loss shall be specially allocated to the Members in accordance with their
         interests in the Company in the event Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) applies, or to the
         Member to whom such distribution was made in the event Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4)
         applies.

         2.       Curative Allocations. The allocations set forth in Section 1 (the “Regulatory Allocations”) are
intended to comply with certain requirements of the Regulations. It is the intent of the Members that, to the extent
possible, all Regulatory Allocations shall be offset either with other Regulatory Allocations or with special
allocations of other items of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction pursuant to this Section 2. Therefore,
notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit (other than the Regulatory Allocations), the Manager shall make
such offsetting special allocations of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction in whatever manner it determines
appropriate so that, after such offsetting allocations are made, each Member's Capital Account balance is, to the
extent possible, equal to the Capital Account balance such Member would have had if the Regulatory Allocations
were not part of this Agreement and all Company items were allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) and Article 6(2). In
exercising their discretion under this Section 2, the Manager shall take into account future Regulatory Allocations
under Sections 1(a) and 1(b) that, although not yet made, are likely to offset other Regulatory Allocations previously
made under Sections 1(e) and 1(f).

         3.        Loss Limitation. Losses allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof shall not exceed the maximum
amount of losses that can be allocated without causing any Member to have an deficit balance in its Capital Account
at the end of any fiscal year. In the event some but not all of the Members would have a deficit balance in its Capital
Account as a consequence of an allocation of losses pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof, the limitation set forth in this
Section 3 shall be applied on a Member by Member basis and losses not allocable to any Member as a result of such
limitation shall be allocated to the other Members in accordance with the positive balances in such Members’
Capital Accounts so as to allocate the maximum permissible losses to each Member under Regulations Section
1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d).

         4.       Other Allocation Rules.

         (a)     For purposes of determining the profits, losses, or any other items allocable to any period, profits,
losses, and any such other items shall be determined on a daily, monthly, or other basis, as determined by the
Manager using any permissible method under Code Section 706 and the Regulations thereunder.

           (b)     Solely for purposes of determining a Member's proportionate share of the "excess nonrecourse
liabilities" of the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.752-3(a)(3), the Members' interests in
Company profits are in proportion to the Membership Interests of such Members.

         (c)     In the event that the Company has taxable income that is characterized as ordinary income under
the recapture provisions of the Code, each Member's distributive share of taxable gain or loss from the sale of
Company assets shall (to the extent possible) include a proportionate share of this recapture income equal to such
Member's share of prior cumulative depreciation deductions with respect to the assets that gave rise to the recapture
income.

          (d)      It is the intention of the parties that the Capital Accounts of the Members immediately before the
liquidation of the Company shall be as nearly equal as possible to the amounts that they would receive in such
liquidation if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions. Therefore, in the fiscal year the Company is liquidated,
should there be any difference between the Capital Accounts of the Members and the amounts they would otherwise
be entitled to receive in liquidation if Article 6(8) governed, then profits and losses in such fiscal year shall be




                                                          13

===== PAGE 1172 =====
specially allocated among the Members so that, to the maximum extent possible, their Capital Accounts shall equal
the amounts to which they would be entitled if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions.

        5.       Tax Allocations: Code Section 704(c). In accordance with Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder, income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to any property contributed to the capital of
the Company shall, solely for tax purposes, be allocated among the Members so as to take account of any variation
between the adjusted basis of such property to the Company for federal income tax purposes and its initial Gross
Asset Value using the "traditional method" pursuant to the Regulations under Code Section 704(c).

         In the event the Gross Asset Value of any Company asset is adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of the
definition of “Gross Asset Value” set forth below, subsequent allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction with
respect to such asset shall take account of any variation between the adjusted basis of such asset for federal income
tax purposes and its Gross Asset Value in the same manner as under Code Section 704(c) and the Regulations
thereunder.

         Any elections or other decisions relating to such allocations shall be made by the Manager in any manner
that reasonably reflects the purpose and intention of this Agreement. Allocations pursuant to this Section 5 are solely
for purposes of federal, state, and local taxes and shall not affect, or in any way be taken into account in computing,
any Member's Capital Account or share of profits, losses, other items, or distributions pursuant to any provision of
this Agreement.

For purposes of this Exhibit A, the following definitions shall apply:

         (i)      “Company Minimum Gain” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partnership minimum
gain” in Sections 1.704-2(b)(2) and 1.704-2(d) of the Regulations.

         (ii)     “Company Nonrecourse Debt” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner nonrecourse
debt” in Section 1.704-2(b)(4) of the Regulations.

         (iii)    “Company Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain” means an amount, with respect to each Member
Nonrecourse Debt, equal to the Company Minimum Gain that would result if such Member Nonrecourse Debt were
treated as a Nonrecourse Liability, determined in accordance with Section 1.704-2(i)(3) of the Regulations.

        (iv)    “Company Nonrecourse Deductions” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner
nonrecourse deductions” in Sections 1.704-2(i)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(2) of the Regulations.

         (v)      “Gross Asset Value” means, with respect to any asset, the asset's adjusted basis for federal income
tax purposes, except as follows:

                  (i) The initial Gross Asset Value of any asset contributed by a Member to the Company shall be
         the gross fair market value of such asset, as determined by the contributing Member and the Manager.

                  (ii) The Gross Asset Values of all Company assets shall be adjusted to equal their respective gross
         fair market values, as determined by the Manager, as of the following times: (a) the acquisition of an
         additional interest in the Company by any new or existing Member in exchange for more than a de minimis
         Capital Contribution; (b) the distribution by the Company to any Member of more than a de minimis
         amount of property as consideration for an interest in the Company; and (c) the liquidation of the Company
         within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g); provided, however, that adjustments
         pursuant to clauses (a) and (b) above shall be made only if the Manager reasonably determines that such
         adjustments are necessary or appropriate to reflect the relative economic interests of the Members in the
         Company.

                  (iii) The Gross Asset Value of any Company asset distributed to any Member shall be adjusted to
         equal the gross fair market value of such asset on the date of distribution as determined by the distributee
         and the Manager.

                   (iv)     The Gross Asset Values of Company assets shall be increased (or decreased) to reflect
         any adjustments to the adjusted basis of such assets pursuant to Code Section 734(b) or Section 743(b), but
         only to the extent that such adjustments are taken into account in determining Capital Accounts pursuant to
         Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m) and subparagraph (vi) of the definition of “Profits” and “Losses”
         set forth in this definition of “Gross Asset Value”, or pursuant to Section 1(e) hereof; provided, however,
         that Gross Asset Values shall not be adjusted pursuant to this subparagraph (iv) to the extent that an
         adjustment pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of this definition is required in connection with a transaction that
         would otherwise result in an adjustment pursuant to this subparagraph (iv).

If the Gross Asset Value of an asset has been determined or adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (i), subparagraph (ii), or
subparagraph (iv) of this definition, such Gross Asset Value shall thereafter be adjusted by the depreciation taken into
account with respect to such asset for purposes of computing profits and losses.

         (vi)     “Nonrecourse Deductions” has the meaning set forth in Section 1.704-2(b)(1) of the Regulations.

         (vii)    “Nonrecourse Liability” has the meaning set forth in Section 1.704-2(b)(3) of the Regulations.

OPERATING AGREEMENT
OF
QUINTO DELTA LLC

THIS OPERATING AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of July 10, 2019 by
TRYKO DELTA HOLDINGS, LLC (“Tryko”) and NORMAN ROKEACH, an individual (“Rokeach”).

In consideration of the mutual covenants herein contained, the Members hereby enter into this Operating
Agreement to control the operations of Quinto Delta LLC, a limited liability company formed under and pursuant to
the laws of the State of New Jersey (hereinafter sometimes referred to as the “Company”) for the purposes and upon
the terms, provisions and conditions hereinafter set forth. This Agreement supersedes and replaces in its entirety
any prior version of the operating agreement for the Company.

Unless the context shall clearly indicate otherwise, all words and phrases used in this Company Agreement
shall have the meaning set forth in the New Jersey Limited Liability Company Act, the “Act”).

ARTICLE 1
FORMATION

1. Name. The name of the Company shall be Quinto Delta LLC.

2. Place of Business. The principal place of business of the Company shall 1608 Route 88, Suite 301,
Brick, New Jersey or such other place or places as the Manager may from time to time designate.

3. Formation; Ratification. The Company was formed by the filing of the Certificate of Formation on
July 10,2019. The Members do hereby ratify and authorize any and all actions taken in the name of the Company
since the date of formation.

4. Member’s Authority. Except as otherwise expressly and specifically provided for in this Agreement
or in the Certificate of Formation, no Member shall have any authority to act for, or assume any obligations or
responsibility on behalf of, the Company or any other Member of the Company.

5. Member’s Prior Obligations. No Member shall be responsible or liable for any obligation or debt of
any other Member incurred before the formation of the Company except as may be set forth herein, and each party
indemnifies and agrees to hold all others harmless from such obligations and indebtedness.

6. Other Business. Nothing herein shall restrict any Member from conducting any other business or
activity whatsoever (including any operation or business or activity which competes with the business of the
Company).

7. Registered Agent. The registered agent for the Company shall be Business Services Plus LLC, at
1608 Route 88, Suite 301, Brick, NJ 08724.

8. Term. The Company shall continue until the earliest to occur of the sale or other disposition of all or
substantially all of the property of the Company, the incompetence or permanent disability of the sole remaining
Member or upon the approval of the Manager and two-thirds (2/3) of all of the Membership Interests.

9. Purposes of the Company. The purpose of the Company shall be to engage in any business in which
a limited liability company may lawfully engage pursuant to the Act and to own the Property.

10. Powers of the Company. The Company shall at any time and from time to time have the power and
authority to do or cause to be done all things necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes of the Company
described in Section 1(9) hereof, including, but not limited to acquiring or disposing of real or personal (or mixed)
property or any interest therein and manage property for others, obtaining financing for the Company, including
refinancing and further including interim and permanent financing (and refinancing) for the acquisition and
development of real property and financing the operations of the Company, sell or transfer or mortgage or place (or
suffer to be placed) an encumbrance on any property of the Company, enter into leases or other similar arrangements,
construct, reconstruct, alter, maintain, repair and demolish improvements on or to any real property of the Company,

ARTICLE 4
CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS

1. Initial Capital Contributions. All Capital Contributions of the Company shall be contributed in
accordance with the Membership Interests of the Members, provided that Rokeach shall not be obligated to make
any Capital Contributions unless Rokeach has such obligation pursuant to the Quinto Agreement. The Manager
does not, in any way, guarantee the return of the Members’ Capital Contributions or a profit for the Members from
the operations of the Company. In addition to the Capital Contributions of the Members, upon acquisition of the
Company’s property, the Company may borrow additional funds from all of the Members or an affiliate of the
Company which loan shall be evidenced by a note and shall be repaid as set forth therein.

2. Estimated Expenses. The Manager shall, from time to time, but not more often than quarterly,
estimate the cash requirements of the Company for an ensuing period of time and the Members shall each be
responsible to pay their pro rata share of such estimated cash requirements in accordance with the Members’
Membership Interests.

3. Members Failure to Make Contributions. Upon demand by the Manager, each Member agrees to
pay, within ten (10) days after receiving a demand therefore, its pro rata share (based upon such Member’s interest
in the Company pursuant to Section 3(1) and irrespective of the percentage of the Initial Capital Contributions of
each Member) of all costs, expenses or charges with respect to the ownership, construction, operation, maintenance
and upkeep of the Company’s property to the extent that all of said costs, expenses or charges cannot be paid out of
the cash flow (as herein defined) if any, of the Company, provided, however, that Rokeach’s obligation to make the
Capital Call is subject to the provisions of the Quinto Agreement. The provisions of this paragraph shall be binding
upon the Members and the Company, but such provisions shall not inure to the benefit of any other person including
any creditors of the Company. Any distribution due to a Member who has defaulted in payment of any required
Capital Contribution shall be first applied to any reimbursement owed by that defaulting Member to the Company
plus interest at the rate agreed to by the parties, which shall compound monthly, pursuant to the heter iska in Section
9(12) below (the “Heter Iska”), or to another Member who has made the Capital Contributions on the part of the
defaulting Member plus interest as provided for in Section 5 of this Article, before distribution of the remainder, if
any, to the defaulting Member.

4. Option to Assist Defaulting Member. If any Member shall default in the payment of any sums
required to be paid by it to the Company hereunder (the “Defaulting Member”), the Manager shall notify the other
Members regarding such default and the other Members may (the “Assisting Member”), without the Company
waiving any claims for breach, cure such default for the account of the Defaulting Member (the “Default Loan’).
The Defaulting Member shall be responsible to repay (solely out of any distribution to which the defaulting Member
may be entitled) the Default Loan with interest at the rate agreed to by the parties which shall compound monthly
and shall be subject to the Heter Iska. Until the Default Loan is repaid in full with interest as herein provided, all
distributions which would otherwise have been made to the Defaulting Member shall be paid to the Assisting
Member, to be applied first to accrued interest and then to principal. Any distribution to the Assisting Member in
connection with the Default Loan pursuant to this Paragraph (or to the Company pursuant to Section 4 of this Article)
shall be considered a distribution to the Defaulting Member. In the event more than one Member wishes to make

io)

interest each such Assisting Member has to the combined Membership Interests of all Assisting Members. All

5. Priority of Capital Contributions. Except as may be expressly provided in this Agreement, no

any payments on such loan shall be first used to pay interest and then to principal.

notice to the Manager of such allegation and the Manager shall have sixty (60) days to cure said Bad Act. In the
event that the Bad Act is not cured within the time set forth herein and the Manager is terminated from providing
services, the Company shall hire a third party to provide such services to the Company.

11. Resignation. The Manager may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Members of the
Company. The resignation of the Manager shall take effect upon receipt of the notice or at such later time as shall
be specified in the notice; and, unless otherwise specified in the notice, the acceptance of the resignation shall not be
necessary to make it effective. The resignation of a Manager who is also a Member shall not affect the Manager’s
rights as a Member and shall not constitute a withdrawal of a Member.

12. Removal and Replacement. The Manager may not be removed except upon an affirmative vote of
Members owning more than two-thirds (2/3) of the Membership Interests of the Company. Any vacancy occurring
for any reason in the office of Manager for any reason shall be filled by the vote of two-thirds (2/3) of the Members.
A Manager elected to fill a vacancy shall be elected for the unexpired term of the Manager’s predecessor in office
and shall hold office until a successor shall be elected and shall qualify, or until the Manager’s earlier death,
resignation, or removal. The managing director and other officers may be removed at any time by the Manager and
any vacancy in the office of managing director or other officer position shall be filled by the Manager.

and after hypothetically increasing such Capital Account balances by amounts of any Company Minimum Gain
and Member Minimum Gain that would be allocated to the Members if all Company assets were sold for an
amount equal to the Company indebtedness encumbering such assets) were distributed to the Members in the
order and priority specified in subsections (6) of this Article,

2. Allocation of Losses. Items of net loss and deduction shall be allocated among the Members in the
manner necessary to reduce each Member’s Capital Account to an amount equal to the amount of cash such Member
would be entitled to receive pursuant to subsections (6) of this Article if an amount of cash equal to the net positive
Capital Account balances after such allocation and after hypothetically increasing such Capital Account balances by
amounts of any Company Minimum Gain and Member Minimum Gain that would be allocated to the Members if
all Company assets were sold for an amount equal to the Company indebtedness encumbering such assets) were
distributed to the Members in the order and priority specified in subsections (6) of this Article.

3. Other Allocations. It is the intention of the Members that allocations of profits and losses made to
the Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code
Section 704(b). The provisions of Section 6(1) and Section 6(2) shall be interpreted consistent with, and subject
to, the terms set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto, which terms shall be incorporated herein as if restated in
full in this Article 6, as applicable to the operations of the Company.

4. Capital Accounts. Each Member shall have a Capital Account which shall consist of its
(a) Capital Contributions to the capital of the Company;
(b) Plus, the amount of profits allocated to it pursuant to Section 6(1);
(c) Minus, the amount of losses associated to it pursuant to Section 6(2); and,

(d) Minus, all amounts paid or distributed to such Member pursuant hereto;

5. Interest on Capital Accounts. No interest shall be paid or accrued on any Member’s Capital Account
except as herein provided.

6. Distributions. All distributions of the Company shall be distributed to the Members in the following
order of priority subject to the provisions of Section 7 of this Article, below:

a) to Tryko to pay any preferred return to which Tryko is entitled;

b) to the Members in accordance with and in proportion to each Member’s capital contribution
in the Company until each Member receives the total amount of its capital contributions;

c) to the Members in accordance with the Members’ Membership Interests in the Company as
provided in Section 3(1).

Prior to any distribution of cash flow arising from the sale or disposition of all or substantially all of the Company’s
property, the Company shall first apply such cash flow to the payment of any unpaid expenses and outstanding loans
of the Company prior to the distributions set forth in this subsection.

7. Repayment to Quinto. Rokeach agrees that all amounts that are to be distributed to Rokeach pursuant
to Section 6 of this Article, should be paid directly to Quinto Holdings LLC as a capital contribution to Quinto
Holdings by Rokeach until such time as Rokeach is entitled to distributions in accordance with the Quinto

===== PAGE 1185 =====
[OCR]
Agreement. All such amounts shall be considered distributions to Rokeach for purposes of allocating profits and
losses of the Company. .

ARTICLE 7
TRANSFER OF INTEREST

1. Prohibition Against Transfer. Except as hereinafter set forth, no Member may sell, assign, transfer,
encumber or otherwise dispose of all or any part of the property of the Company or its interest in the Company
whether direct or indirect through any number of tiers without the consent of the Manager which consent may be
withheld in its sole and absolute discretion. It is the intent of this section to maintain the control of the Company in
the natural persons who own the Company on the Effective Date. Any transfer not in accordance with this Article
7 shall have no effect and will not be recognized by the Company. Upon the death of any individual who has interest
in the Company on the date that the Company initially acquires the property, such interest shall devise to his heirs.

2. Assignment by Members. Any Member shall have the right to transfer or assign all or part of its share
to a subsidiary or affiliated company or to an entity in which the Member is the Manager or controlling party with
full control of all aspects of the entity (hereinafter a “Permitted Assignee”). Any Member or any Permitted Assignee
may also transfer or assign part, but not all, of its or their share to individuals who control that Member or any
Permitted Assignee, to heir lineal descendants (hereinafter “Family Members”), or to any or all of the foregoing;
provided, however, transfers or assignments to Family Members shall not include any voting rights, which voting
rights shall be reserved by the Member or the Permitted Assignee which is making the transfer or assignment to the
Family Member.

3. Assumption by Assignee. Any assignee or transferee who acquires all or part of a share in the
Company pursuant to the terms of this Agreement or otherwise shall take such share subject to all of the terms and
conditions of this Agreement; and such person shall not be considered to have such share until he shall agree in
writing to assume the obligations of his assignor or transfer hereunder and if such person is not at the time of such
transfer a party to this Agreement, to otherwise be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

4. No Right to Force Assignment. Neither party shall have the right to force the other party to sell its
interests to the other in any court or other proceeding.

ARTICLE 8
DISSOLUTION

1. Termination or Dissolution. Upon termination of the Company, the Company shall be dissolved and
its affairs and business shall be liquidated forthwith. All property of the Company shall be sold or otherwise disposed
of and the new proceeds therefor, if any, and the remaining assets of the Company shall be applied first to satisfy the
costs, expenses, charges and liabilities of the Company, either by payment or the establishment of an adequate
reserve to cover the same and the balance shall be distributed to the Members in accordance with the distribution
provisions of this Agreement.

2. Tax Effect of Termination or Dissolution. It is the intention of the Members that allocations made
to the Members have economic effect equivalence in accordance with the regulations under Internal Revenue Code
Section 704(b). The provisions of this Section 8(2) shall be interpreted consistent with, and subject to, the terms
set forth on Exhibit A attached hereto, which terms shall be incorporated herein as if restated in full in this
Article 8, as applicable to the termination and dissolution of the Company. If a Member has a deficit balance in
its Capital Account (after giving effect to all contributions, distributions, and allocations for all tax years,
including the tax year in which such liquidation occurs), such Member shall have no obligation to make any
contribution to the capital of the Company with respect to such deficit, and such deficit shall not be considered
a debt owed to the Company or to any other Person for any purpose whatsoever.

3. Dissolution Procedure. Within thirty (30) days of the termination of the Company or an event of
Dissolution as set forth in this Agreement, the Manager shall retain the services of a qualified appraiser to value all

===== PAGE 1186 =====
[OCR]
of the property of the Company. The assets of the Company shall be distributed to the Members if practical and if
acceptable to all Members, or sold at prices in accordance with said appraisal.

4. Continuation. Nothing contained herein shall be construed as limiting the ability of the remaining
Members from execution of a new Agreement and continuing the business of the Company, all in accordance with
the Act and the applicable provision of the Code.

5. Events of Dissolution. The Company shall dissolve and commence to wind up its affairs upon the
occurrence of any of the following, in addition to those set forth elsewhere herein (each a “Dissolution Event”):

(a) The written consent of the manager and the members holding three quarters (3/4) of all of the
Membership Interests to dissolve;

(b) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under Section 18-802 of the Act; or

(c) Ninety (90) days after the date on which the Company no longer has at least one Member,
unless at least one new Member is admitted to the Company within such 90-day period by such Member’s
legal representative.

The Members hereby agree that, notwithstanding any provision of the Act, the Company shall not dissolve
prior to the occurrence of a Dissolution Event. For avoidance of doubt, any event that terminates the
continued membership of any Member shall not cause the Company to be dissolved or its affairs to be
wound up, and upon the occurrence of any such event, the Company shall be continued without dissolution.

ARTICLE 9
MISCELLANEOUS

1. Property Manager. Upon agreement of the Managers, a property management company shall be
hired for the management of any real property owned by the Company. Any property management agreement shall
be in writing, and shall include a provision that the agreement may be terminated upon one full calendar month’s
written notice. Any Member may have an ownership or controlling interest in the chosen property management
company. The Management Fee paid to the Manager shall be reduced by any amount paid to a third party
management company.

2. Members Consent. The Company is not required to hold any meetings. Whenever the consent or the
vote of the Members is required in this Agreement, the Manager shall notify all of the Members of the need for
consent or a vote, which notice may be via email and a phone conversation to each Member. Such consent shall be
deemed granted and such vote shall be deemed approved upon the receipt by the Manager of the required amount of
affirmative email responses by Members representing the required amount of Membership Interests for such consent
as set forth in this Agreement. In the event that the percentage of the Company Interest required for a specific action
is not specified in this Agreement, such action shall be approved upon the consent of the majority of the Membership
Interests.

3. Notices. Except as may be otherwise specifically provided for in this Agreement, no notices, requests,
consent, approval, waiver or other communication under this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and
either (a) personally served thereon or (b) sent by regular mail and by certified mail, return receipt requested, with
postage prepaid, or (c) commercial express delivery service providing delivery against receipt, addressed to the
parties at the addresses on file with the Manager, or (d) sent via email to the principal of the Member and such
principal of the Member receiving the notice sends a confirming email.. If personally served or sent via commercial
delivery service, any such matter shall be deemed given for all purposes hereunder at the time of such service or, if
by mail as herein provided, at the time of depositing same in a post office box regularly maintained by the United
States Postal Service. If such notice is sent via email then notice shall be deemed given upon the receipt of the
confirming email.

4. Indemnities. Each Member hereby indemnifies and holds harmless the Manager, the other Members,
and the Company from and against any losses, costs, damages or liabilities which said other Members or the
Company, or both, may suffer or incur as a result of the activities of the indemnifying Member, whether or not
wrongful, outside the scope of this Agreement.

12. Heter Iska. The undersigned members of the Company hereby declare and admit that all advances
made between themselves with respect to capital contributions, loans to the company, capital calls, or any other
mortgages, guarantees, preferred investments, or any other advances, that would violate any of the laws of Ribbis
shall be structured as an Iska investment subject to the following terms. In exchange for the monies advanced, the
recipient/beneficiary shall transfer to the investor a share (of equal value) in his assets as an Iska. In the event that
no such investment exists, or if the recipient participates in a more lucrative investment opportunity in the future, the
recipient shall assign a share of that investment to the investor. This investment shall be owned by the investing
partner, and all profits, capital gains, or losses shall be his sole responsibility. The recipient shall have complete
authority to manage this investment on behalf of the investor, in the manner deemed most beneficial to the investor.
Any investment owned by the recipient may be used to create this Iska, provided that the venture is Halachacly
permissible. This Iska may only be collected from the assets of the Company and the investor shall have no claim
against the personal assets of any of the recipients, unless otherwise specified in an agreement between the parties.
The recipient shall receive five percent of the profits as compensation for his services managing this Iska, and shall
be liable for the monies as a watchman. The recipient must verify any claim of loss through the testimony of two
Halachacly acceptable witnesses in an Orthodox Jewish court of law. Any claim regarding the amount of profits
generated by the joint venture must be verified with a solemn oath, administered by an Orthodox Jewish court of
law. In addition, the investor may demand full access to all legal records, documents, financial statements or receipts
that the investor deems necessary to verify the claims of the recipient. In the event of a claim of loss, the investor
may demand a full and immediate payment of the remaining balance of this Iska. It is agreed that if the recipient
pays the amount equal to the principal, interest, penalties, default rates, preferred returns, membership dilution,
buyout rights, or other benefits called for by this Agreement, as per the payment schedule of this Agreement, as
payment for the investor's share of the principal and profits of the Iska investment, the investor shall waive his right
to demand verification of the results of the investment. Any additional profits shall belong solely to the recipient.
Such payment shall reflect a final settlement, and the recipient shall have no further claim for compensation,
management or services fees, unless specified to the contrary in other agreements executed between the parties. Any
payments made that are not justified by this Iska agreement shall reduce the principal balance of this Iska. However,
any future payments made to avoid providing the abovementioned verification, shall be increased to compensate for
any discrepancy. This section shall override any other section, even those that do not reference this section. Any
mention of loans or interest shall be interpreted as an Iska and to payments mentioned above. This declaration is
legally binding and may be enforced in any Jewish or civil court, even in the event that one of the parties was unaware
of its existence. This agreement has been executed in an effective manner and with a proper Kinyan, if required.

Tax Provisions
Special Allocations. The following special allocations shall be made in the following order:

(a) Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations Section
1.704-2(f), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in Company
Minimum Gain during any fiscal year, each Member shall be specially allocated items of Company
income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to
such Member's share of the net decrease in Company Minimum Gain, determined in accordance with
Regulations Section 1.704-2(g). Allocations pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in
proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The
items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Regulations Sections 1.704-2(f)(6) and
1.704-2(j)(2). This Section 1(a) is intended to comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement
in Regulations Section 1.704-2(f) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

(b) Member Minimum Gain Chargeback. Except as otherwise provided in Regulations
Section 1.704-2(i)(4), notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit, if there is a net decrease in
Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to a Member Nonrecourse Debt during any
fiscal year, each Member who has a share of the Member Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable
to such Member Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(5),
shall be specially allocated items of Company income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary,
subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Member's share of the net decrease in Member
Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4). Allocations
pursuant to the previous sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be
allocated to each Member pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in
accordance with Regulations Sections 1.704-2(i)(4) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This Section 1(b) is intended to
comply with the minimum gain chargeback requirement in Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(4) and shall
be interpreted consistently therewith.

(c) Qualified Income Offset. In the event any Member unexpectedly receives any
adjustments, allocations, or distributions described in Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4),
Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(5), or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(6), items of Company income and gain
shall be specially allocated to such Member in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate, to the
extent required by the Regulations, the deficit balance in the Capital Account of such Member as quickly
as possible, provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(c) shall be made only if and to the
extent that such Member would have an deficit balance in its Capital Account after all other allocations
provided for in this Exhibit have been tentatively made as if this Section 1(c) were not in this Exhibit.

(d) Gross Income Allocation. In the event any Member has a deficit Capital Account at
the end of any fiscal year that is in excess of the amount such Member is obligated to restore pursuant
to the penultimate sentences of Regulations Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(5), such Member
shall be specially allocated items of Company income and gain in the amount of such excess as quickly
as possible, provided, that an allocation pursuant to this Section 1(d) shall be made only if and to the
extent that such Member would have a deficit Capital Account in excess of such amount after all other
allocations provided for in this Exhibit have been made as if Section 1(c) and this Section 1(d) were not
in this Agreement.

(e) Nonrecourse Deductions. Nonrecourse Deductions for any fiscal year shall be
specially allocated to all of the Members in proportion to the Membership Interests of the Members.

(f) Member Nonrecourse Deductions. Any Member Nonrecourse Deductions for any
fiscal year shall be specially allocated to the Member who bears the economic risk of loss with respect

to the Member Nonrecourse Debt to which such Member Nonrecourse Deductions are attributable in
accordance with Regulations Section 1.704-2(i)(1).

(g) Section 754 Adjustments. To the extent an adjustment to the adjusted tax basis of any
Company asset pursuant to Code Section 734(b) or Section 743(b) is required, pursuant to Regulations
Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) or Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4), to be taken into account in
determining Capital Accounts as the result of a distribution to a Member in complete liquidation of such
Member's interest in the Company, the amount of such adjustment to the Capital Accounts shall be
treated as an item of gain (if the adjustment increases the basis of the asset) or as an item of loss (if the
adjustment decreases such basis), and such gain or loss shall be specially allocated to the Members in

applies, or to the Member to whom such distribution was made in the event Regulations Section
1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4) applies.

2. Curative Allocations. The allocations set forth in Section 1 (the “Regulatory Allocations”)
are intended to comply with certain requirements of the Regulations. It is the intent of the Members that, to the
extent possible, all Regulatory Allocations shall be offset either with other Regulatory Allocations or with special
allocations of other items of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction pursuant to this Section 2. Therefore,
notwithstanding any other provision of this Exhibit (other than the Regulatory Allocations), the Manager shall
make such offsetting special allocations of Company income, gain, loss, or deduction in whatever manner it
determines appropriate so that, after such offsetting allocations are made, each Member's Capital Account
balance is, to the extent possible, equal to the Capital Account balance such Member would have had if the
Regulatory Allocations were not part of this Agreement and all Company items were allocated pursuant to
Article 6(1) and Article 6(2). In exercising their discretion under this Section 2, the Manager shall take into
account future Regulatory Allocations under Sections 1(a) and 1(b) that, although not yet made, are likely to
offset other Regulatory Allocations previously made under Sections 1(e) and 1(f).

3; Loss Limitation. Losses allocated pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof shall not exceed the
maximum amount of losses that can be allocated without causing any Member to have an deficit balance in its
Capital Account at the end of any fiscal year. In the event some but not all of the Members would have a deficit
balance in its Capital Account as a consequence of an allocation of losses pursuant to Article 6(1) hereof, the
limitation set forth in this Section 3 shall be applied on a Member by Member basis and losses not allocable to
any Member as a result of such limitation shall be allocated to the other Members in accordance with the positive
balances in such Members’ Capital Accounts so as to allocate the maximum permissible losses to each Member
under Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(@).

4, Other Allocation Rules.

(a) For purposes of determining the profits, losses, or any other items allocable to any period,
profits, losses, and any such other items shall be determined on a daily, monthly, or other basis, as determined
by the Manager using any permissible method under Code Section 706 and the Regulations thereunder.

(b) Solely for purposes of determining a Member's proportionate share of the "excess nonrecourse
liabilities" of the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.752-3(a)(3), the Members' interests in
Company profits are in proportion to the Membership Interests of such Members.

(c) In the event that the Company has taxable income that is characterized as ordinary income
under the recapture provisions of the Code, each Member's distributive share of taxable gain or loss from the
sale of Company assets shall (to the extent possible) include a proportionate share of this recapture income equal
to such Member's share of prior cumulative depreciation deductions with respect to the assets that gave rise to
the recapture income.

(d) It is the intention of the parties that the Capital Accounts of the Members immediately before
the liquidation of the Company shall be as nearly equal as possible to the amounts that they would receive in
such liquidation if Article 6(8) governed liquidating distributions. Therefore, in the fiscal year the Company is

liquidated, should there be any difference between the Capital Accounts of the Members and the amounts they
would otherwise be entitled to receive in liquidation if Article 6(8) governed, then profits and losses in such
fiscal year shall be specially allocated among the Members so that, to the maximum extent possible, their Capital
Accounts shall equal the amounts to which they would be entitled if Article 6(8) governed liquidating
distributions.

5. Tax Allocations: Code Section 704(c). In accordance with Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder, income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to any property contributed to the capital
of the Company shall, solely for tax purposes, be allocated among the Members so as to take account of any
variation between the adjusted basis of such property to the Company for federal income tax purposes and its
initial Gross Asset Value using the "traditional method" pursuant to the Regulations under Code Section 704(c).

In the event the Gross Asset Value of any Company asset is adjusted pursuant to subparagraph (ii) of
the definition of “Gross Asset Value” set forth below, subsequent allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction
with respect to such asset shall take account of any variation between the adjusted basis of such asset for federal
income tax purposes and its Gross Asset Value in the same manner as under Code Section 704(c) and the
Regulations thereunder.

Any elections or other decisions relating to such allocations shall be made by the Manager in any
manner that reasonably reflects the purpose and intention of this Agreement. Allocations pursuant to this Section
5 are solely for purposes of federal, state, and local taxes and shall not affect, or in any way be taken into account
in computing, any Member's Capital Account or share of profits, losses, other items, or distributions pursuant to
any provision of this Agreement.

For purposes of this Exhibit A, the following definitions shall apply:

(i) “Company Minimum Gain” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partnership
minimum gain” in Sections 1.704-2(b)(2) and 1.704-2(d) of the Regulations.

(ii) “Company Nonrecourse Debt” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner
nonrecourse debt” in Section 1.704-2(b)(4) of the Regulations.

(iii) “Company Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain” means an amount, with respect to each Member
Nonrecourse Debt, equal to the Company Minimum Gain that would result if such Member Nonrecourse Debt
were treated as a Nonrecourse Liability, determined in accordance with Section 1.704-2(i)(3) of the Regulations.

(iv) “Company Nonrecourse Deductions” has the same meaning as is given to the term “partner
nonrecourse deductions” in Sections 1.704-2(i)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(2) of the Regulations.

(v) “Gross Asset Value” means, with respect to any asset, the asset's adjusted basis for federal
income tax purposes, except as follows:

(i) The initial Gross Asset Value of any asset contributed by a Member to the Company shall
be the gross fair market value of such asset, as determined by the contributing Member and the Manager.

(ii) The Gross Asset Values of all Company assets shall be adjusted to equal their respective
gross fair market values, as determined by the Manager, as of the following times: (a) the acquisition
of an additional interest in the Company by any new or existing Member in exchange for more than a
de minimis Capital Contribution; (b) the distribution by the Company to any Member of more than a de
minimis amount of property as consideration for an interest in the Company; and (c) the liquidation of
the Company within the meaning of Regulations Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g); provided, however, that
adjustments pursuant to clauses (a) and (b) above shall be made only if the Manager reasonably
determines that such adjustments are necessary or appropriate to reflect the relative economic interests
of the Members in the Company.

Independent Auditors’ Report

To the Members

80 Douglas Pike, LLC

d/b/a Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center
Smithfield, Rhode Island

We have audited the accompanying financial statements of 80 Douglas Pike, LLC d/b/a
Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center, which comprise the balance sheet as of
December 31, 2018 and the related statements of income and members’ equity and cash
flows for the year then ended, and the related notes to the financial statements.

Management’s Responsibility for the Financial Statements

Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of these financial
statements in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United
States of America; this includes the design, implementation and maintenance of internal
control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of financial statements that are free
from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

Auditors’ Responsibility

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audit.
We conducted our audit in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the
United States of America. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to
obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free from material
misstatement.

An audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit evidence about the amounts and
disclosures in the financial statements. The procedures selected depend on the auditors’
judgment, including the assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the financial
statements, whether due to fraud or error. In making those risk assessments, the auditors
consider internal control relevant to the entity's preparation and fair presentation of the
financial statements in order to design audit procedures that are appropriate in the
circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the
entity’s internal control. Accordingly, we express no such opinion. An audit also includes
evaluating the appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of
significant accounting estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall
presentation of the financial statements.

We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide
a basis for our audit opinion.

NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

NOTE 1 - NATURE OF BUSINESS

80 Douglas Pike, LLC d/b/a Heritage Hills Nursing & Rehabilitation Center (the Company) operates as
a 100-bed nursing facility located in Smithfield, Rhode Island. The Company is licensed by the Rhode
Island Department of Health and participates in the Medicaid and Medicare programs.

The members of the Company have limited liability to creditors and other third parties. The Company
has an indefinite life and shall only be dissolved in accordance with its operating agreement.

NOTE 2 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
Use of Estimates

The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in
the United States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the
reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date
of the financial statements. Estimates also affect the reported amounts of revenues and expenses
during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.

Cash and Cash Equivalents

The Company considers all highly liquid investments with a maturity of three months or less to be cash
equivalents.

Accounts Receivable

The Company carries its accounts receivable at cost less an allowance for doubtful accounts of
$186,000 at December 31, 2018. On a periodic basis, the Company evaluates its accounts receivable
and establishes an allowance for doubtful accounts based on a history of past write-offs, collections
and current credit conditions. Accounts are written off based on management's evaluation of the
collectibilty of each account resulting from collection efforts.

Property, Equipment and Depreciation

Property and equipment are recorded at cost. Depreciation is calculated on the straight-line method
over the expected useful lives of the assets.

Impairment of Long-Lived Assets

The Company reviews long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances
indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable. Recoverability of assets to be
held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset to estimated future
cash flows expected to be generated by the asset. If the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its
estimated future cash flows, an impairment charge is recognized for the amount by which the carrying
amount of the asset exceeds the fair value of the asset.

===== PAGE 1206 =====
[OCR]
80 DOUGLAS PIKE, LLC
D/B/A HERITAGE HILLS NURSING & REHABILITATION CENTER

NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

Goodwill

Goodwill is recognized as a result of a business combination when the price paid for the acquired
business exceeds the fair value of the tangible and identifiable intangible assets. Accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America require that goodwill not be amortized, but rather
tested for impairment at least annually. Management has determined that goodwill is not impaired as of
December 31, 2018.

Net Patient Service Revenue

Net patient service revenue is reported at the estimated net realizable amounts from patients,
third-party payors, and others for services rendered. Revenue consists primarily of reimbursement
through the Medicaid and Medicare programs as well as revenue from private paying patients.
Revenue from the Medicare and Medicaid programs accounted for approximately 11% and 58%,
respectively, of the Company's net patient service revenue for the year ended December 31, 2018.

Certain regulations under third-party reimbursement provisions may allow for a_ retroactive
reimbursement or payment which is recorded as an estimated third-party settlement in the period
earned or incurred. Differences between estimated amounts accrued and actual settlements are
reported as a settlement adjustment in the year the final settlement is received or paid. Management
believes that all applicable government reimbursement principles have been properly applied and that
no material adjustments will occur as a result of an audit.

Income Taxes

The Company has elected to be taxed as a partnership under the provisions of the Internal Revenue
Code. Under those provisions, the Company is not required to pay federal and state income taxes on
its taxable income. Instead, the members are liable for individual federal and state income taxes on
their respective shares of the Company’s taxable income.

Accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America require management to
evaluate tax positions taken by the Company and recognize a tax liability if the Company has taken an
uncertain position that more likely than not would not be sustained upon examination by the Internal
Revenue Service. Management believes that no uncertain tax positions exist as of December 31,
2018. The Company is subject to routine audits by taxing jurisdictions; however, there are currently no
audits for any tax periods in progress. The Company recognizes interest and penalties, if applicable,
as a component of supplies and other expenses.

Subsequent Events

Subsequent events have been evaluated through April 10, 2019, the date the financial statements are
available to be issued.

NOTE 5 - DUE TO THIRD-PARTY PAYORS

Amounts due to third-party payors represents overpayments and funding advanced by the Rhode
Island Medicaid program to provide working capital while the State of Rhode Island addresses delays in
the processing of Medicaid claims.

NOTE 6 - RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS
Management Fees

Management fees charged by Health Concepts, Ltd., a company related by common ownership, were
based upon a fee of up to 7% of net patient revenues. Management fees incurred and paid were
$546,170 and $831,180 for the year ended December 31, 2018. As of December 31, 2018,
management fees in the amount of $24,234 have been prepaid and are included in prepaid expenses
and other current assets on the balance sheet.

Maintenance and Administrative Services and General Insurance Programs

Health Concepts, Ltd., provides maintenance and administrative services to the Company. In addition,
general insurance coverage is provided through Health Concepts, Ltd’s package policy. Services and
insurance costs incurred and paid for the year ended December 31, 2018 were $154,679.

Self-Insurance Health Plan

The Company participates in a self-insurance health plan that was established by Health Concepts,
Ltd., and provides health coverage for employees. Self-insurance costs are accrued based on claims
reported as of the balance sheet date as well as an estimated liability for claims incurred but not
reported. The health plan carries a stop-loss insurance policy with a commercial insurance carrier to
protect the health plan assets from individual losses in excess of $100,000. The total health insurance
costs incurred for the self-insured component of the plan for the year ended December 31, 2018 totaled
$375,816. As of December 31, 2018, the Company had prepaid premiums in the amount $64,363,
which were included in prepaid expenses and other current assets on the balance sheet.

NOTE 7 - HEALTHCARE INDUSTRY
Regulatory Environment

The healthcare industry is subject to numerous laws and regulations of federal, state and local
governments. These laws and regulations include, but are not necessarily limited to, matters such as
licensure, accreditation, government healthcare program participation requirements, reimbursement for
patient services, and Medicare fraud and abuse. Government activity has increased with respect to
investigations and allegations concerning possible violations of fraud and abuse statutes and
regulations by healthcare providers. Violations of these laws and regulations could result in expulsion
from government healthcare programs together with the imposition of significant fines and penalties, as
well as significant repayments for patient services previously billed. Management believes that the
Company is in compliance with fraud and abuse regulations as well as other applicable government
laws and regulations. While no material regulatory inquiries have been made in 2018, compliance with
such laws and regulations can be subject to future government review and interpretation, as well as
regulatory actions unknown or unasserted at this time.

In a prior year, the Company was a party to a settlement agreement with the United States Department
of Justice, Office of Inspector General (OIG), in which the Company paid an agreed-upon balance
relating to previously submitted therapy claims for the period June 1, 2012 through December 31, 2015.
In addition, as part of the settlement agreement, the Company became a party to a Corporate Integrity
Agreement (CIA) with the OIG. The CIA requires that Health Concepts, Ltd., establish and maintain a
Compliance Program that promotes adherence with Medicare and Medicaid regulations, for all skilled
nursing facilities owned, operated, affiliated with or managed by Health Concepts, Ltd., including the
Company. The CIA is for a five-year period commencing September 2016. During the year ended
December 31, 2017, the OIG accepted the Annual Report submitted by Health Concepts, Ltd., pursuant
to the CIA. Health Concepts, Ltd., believes they are in compliance with the requirements of the CIA as
of December 31, 2018.

Goodwill

Goodwill is recognized as a result of a business combination when the price paid for the acquired
business exceeds the fair value of the tangible and identifiable intangible assets. Accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America require that goodwill not be amortized, but rather

Debt Issuance Costs

Debt issuance costs are bank fees and other costs incurred in obtaining financing that are amortized on

expense.

Paycheck Protection Program

The Company has elected to account for the loan received under the Paycheck Protection Program
(PPP) as a debt instrument in accordance with ASU 470, Debt: Simplifying the Classification of Debt.
Under ASU 470, debt is recognized upon receiving the PPP loan proceeds (see Note 11).

Daily Service Revenue

Daily service revenue is reported at the amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects to
receive (the transaction price) in exchange for providing skilled nursing care. These amounts are due
from residents (private pay), third-party payors (including health insurers and government payors) and
others. Performance obligations are determined based on the nature of the services provided. Daily
service revenue is recognized.as.performance obligations related to skilled nursing services and room
and board are satisfied. The Company recognizes revenue on a per diem basis in accordance with the
provisions of ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Rates charged for services rendered,
other than private-pay residents, are regulated by Medicaid, Medicare and other third-party programs.
Revenue from private-pay residents is based on prevailing rates. Revenue from the Medicare and
Medicaid programs accounted for approximately 14% and 61%, respectively, of the facility's net patient
revenue for the year ended December 31, 2020.

Settlements with third-party payors for retroactive adjustments resulting from audits, reviews or
investigations are included in the determination of the estimated transaction price for providing
services. The Company estimates the transaction price based on the terms of the contract with the
payor, correspondence with the payor and historical payment trends, and retroactive adjustments are
recognized in future periods as final settlements are determined.

The Company has elected the practical expedient under ASC 606 and does not adjust the promised
amount of consideration from patients and third-party payors for the effects of a significant financing
component due to the Company’s expectation that the period between the time the service is provided
to a patient and the time that the patient or a third-party payor pays for that service will be one year or
less. However, the Company does, in certain instances, enter into payment agreements with residents
that allow payments in excess of one year. For those cases, the financing component is not deemed to
be significant to the contract.

Laws and regulations concerning government programs, including Medicare and Medicaid, are complex
and subject to varying interpretation. These laws and regulations include, but are not necessarily
limited to, matters such as licensure, accreditation, government healthcare program participation
requirements (which are a precondition to the receipt of reimbursement for patient services), the
Medicare False Claims Act, the Stark Anti-Referral Act, the Anti-Kickback legislation and other
Medicaid fraud and abuse legislation. Government activity has increased with respect to investigations
that have led to allegations concerning possible violations by healthcare providers of those statutes and
regulations. Violations of these laws and regulations could result in expulsion from government
healthcare programs, together with the imposition of significant fines and penalties, as well as
significant repayments for patient services previously billed and received. Management believes that
the Company is in compliance with fraud and abuse regulations as well as other applicable government
laws and regulations. While no material regulatory inquiries have been made during 2019, compliance
with such laws and regulations can be subject to future government review and interpretation, as well
as regulatory actions unknown or unasserted at this time.

NOTE 4 - INTEREST RATE SWAP CONTRACT AND OTHER FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS

The Company uses derivatives to manage risks related to interest rate movements. The Company's
interest rate risk management strategy is to stabilize cash flow requirements by maintaining interest
rate swap contracts to convert variable debt to a fixed rate. At December 31, 2020, the Company had
an interest rate swap contract as part of the term loan facility related to the mortgage debt with a
notional amount of $5,005,873.

The notional amount decreases each year as principal payments are made. The interest rate swap
contract effectively changes the interest rates on variable rate debt to a fixed rate of 2.365% in 2020.
The contract is a cash flow hedge to eliminate the cash flow exposure of interest rate movements on
variable rate debt throughout the term of the interest rate swap agreements. Interest payments are
settled with the counterparty on a monthly basis which is reflected in interest expense in the
accompanying financial statements. The interest rate swap agreement outstanding at December 31,
2020 matures in August 2029. The Company is subject to exposure to the extent the counterparty to
the contract does not perform under the agreement.

The Company recorded the interest rate swap agreement at fair value at the end of the year, which
because of forecasted levels of LIBOR, resulted in the Company reporting an asset for the fair value of
the future net payments forecasted under the interest rate swap agreement. The fair value of the
interest rate swap agreement was a liability of $389,331 at December 31, 2020. The interest rate swap
agreement is considered to be effective as a hedge, and none of the loss is included in pretax income.
Accordingly, all of the adjustments of the interest rate swap agreement's carrying amounts are reported
as other comprehensive loss.

Accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America establish a framework for
measuring fair value. That framework provides a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to
valuation techniques used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted
quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest
priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3 measurements). This hierarchy prioritizes the inputs into three
broad levels as follows. Level 1 inputs are quoted market prices in active markets for identical assets
or liabilities. Level 2 inputs are quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets or inputs
that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly through market corroboration, for
substantially the full term of the asset or liability. Level 3 inputs are unobservable inputs based on the
Company's own assumptions used to measure assets and liabilities at fair value. An asset or liability’s
classification within the hierarchy is determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the
fair value measurement.

The swap contract is a financial liability measured at fair value on a recurring basis at December 31,
2020 as follows:

NOTE 11 - PAYCHECK PROTECTION PROGRAM

On April 20, 2020, the Company received a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan of $1,085,200
granted by the Small Business Administration (SBA) under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic
Security Act (CARES Act). A portion or all of this loan may be forgivable based on the amount of
qualifying expenses incurred and levels of employee headcount and salaries maintained during a
measurement period. The Company considers the PPP loan to be debt and, accordingly, will record
the amount of forgiveness, if any, when legally released by the lender. The Company has elected the
24-week loan forgiveness period. At the time of issuance of the financial statements, the PPP loan
forgiveness has not been finalized. Any portion of the loan that must be repaid will bear interest at a
rate of 1% per annum. Interest and principal payments on the loan will commence, at a maximum, 10
months after the end of the 24-week loan forgiveness period if the loan has not been forgiven in full, to
be paid in full April 2022. The Company expects the loan to be fully forgiven by the end of 2022,
therefore, the loan is classified as long-term as of December 31, 2020.

NOTE 12 - RISKS AND UNCERTAINTIES

In 2020, the World Health Organization declared the spread of Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) a
worldwide pandemic.

COVID-19 may also impact various parts of the Company's 2021 operations and financial results
including but not limited to additional costs for emergency preparedness, disease control and
containment, potential shortages of health care personnel, or loss of revenue due to reductions in
certain revenue streams. Management believes the Company is taking appropriate actions to mitigate
the negative impact. However, the full impact of COVID-19 is unknown and cannot be reasonably
estimated as of December 31, 2020.
